    10:   diff: "{{ jenkins_show_plugins_yaml_changes }}"

    14:   when: copy_plugins_yaml_file is changed  # noqa no-handler
    15:   block:
    16:     - name: Determine if PIMT output should be logged to a separate file
    17:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    18:         jenkins_pimt_log_output_to_file: true
    19:       when: jenkins_pimt_logfile != ''
    20: 
    21:     - name: Add verbosity argument for PIMT command
    22:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:

    24:       when: ansible_verbosity > 0 or jenkins_pimt_log_output_to_file
    25:

    27:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    28:         jenkins_pimt_args: >-
    29:           {{ jenkins_pimt_args }} 2> /tmp/{{ jenkins_pimt_logfile | basename }}
    30:       when: jenkins_pimt_log_output_to_file
    31: 
    32:     # Remove the plugins directory before installing plugins to avoid potential problems
    33:     # with conflicting dependencies, and also to correctly handle the case when plugins
    34:     # are removed from the plugins.yaml file. PIMT has a `--clean-download-directory`
    35:     # argument, but we can't use it because it'll fail to remove the directory.
    36:     - name: Clean plugins directory
    37:       become: true
    38:       ansible.builtin.file:
    39:         path: "{{ jenkins_plugins_dir }}"
    40:         state: absent
    41: 
    42:     - name: Use PIMT to install plugins
    43:       become: true
    44:       become_user: "{{ jenkins_user }}"
    45:       ansible.builtin.shell:
    46:         cmd: >
    47:           java -jar
    48:           {{ jenkins_pimt_path }}
    49:           --plugin-download-directory {{ jenkins_plugins_dir }}
    50:           --plugin-file {{ jenkins_config_dir }}/plugins.yaml
    51:           --war {{ jenkins_war }}
    52:           {{ jenkins_pimt_args }}
    53:       changed_when: true
    54:       environment:
    55:         CACHE_DIR: "{{ jenkins_caches_dir }}"
    56:       no_log: "{{ jenkins_pimt_log_output_to_file }}"
    57:       retries: "{{ jenkins_download_retries }}"
    58:       delay: "{{ jenkins_download_delay }}"
    59:       register: plugin_installation_result
    60:       until: plugin_installation_result is succeeded
    61: 
    62:     - name: Fetch the PIMT logfile
    63:       ansible.builtin.fetch:
    64:         src: "/tmp/{{ jenkins_pimt_logfile | basename }}"
    65:         dest: "{{ jenkins_pimt_logfile | dirname }}/"
    66:         flat: true
    67:       when: jenkins_pimt_log_output_to_file
    68:   rescue:
    69:     # Because we only run PIMT when the template file changed, we can end up in a bad
    70:     # situation if PIMT fails for other reasons (for instance, a network glitch). This
    71:     # will leave the Jenkins controller in a partially deployed state, and when this role
    72:     # is run again, we need to ensure that PIMT will also be re-run. To do so, we alter
    73:     # the plugins.yaml file, which will ensure that the template task will change it.
    74:     - name: Write failure comment to plugins.yaml file
    75:       become: true

    78:         line: "# Added by Ansible: PIMT failed on last run!"
    79:         insertbefore: BOF
    80:         owner: "{{ jenkins_user }}"
    81:         group: "{{ jenkins_group }}"
    82:         mode: "0644"
    83: 
    84:     - name: Force the play to fail
    85:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    86:         msg: >
    87:           Plugin Installation Manager Tool failed with code
    88:           {{ plugin_installation_result.rc }}: {{ plugin_installation_result.msg }}
    89: 
    90: # We install custom plugins AFTER installing everything else with the plugin installation
    91: # manager tool. This allows us to ensure that these plugins are not overridden by a
    92: # different and possibly conflicting version.
    93: - name: Install custom Jenkins plugins
    94:   become: true
    95:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    96:     src: "{{ plugin_file }}"
    97:     dest: "{{ jenkins_plugins_dir }}"
    98:     owner: "{{ jenkins_user }}"
    99:     group: "{{ jenkins_group }}"
   100:     mode: "0644"
   101:   loop: "{{ jenkins_custom_plugins }}"
   102:   loop_control:
   103:     loop_var: plugin_file

    98:   loop:

   121:     - name: read server.cnf

   123:       register: server_cnf_contents
   124:       changed_when: false

   127:         path: /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf

   133:         - "ssl-cert={{ ssl_cert }}"
   134:         - "ssl-key={{ mariadb_data_folder }}/mysql.server.key"
   135:         - "ssl-ca={{ ssl_ca }}"
   136:       when: not server_cnf_contents.stdout is match('^' + item)
   137:       register: server_cnf_tls
   138:     - name: update server.cnf max_packet property, if needed (Pentaho needs larger packet size)
   139:       lineinfile:
   140:         path: /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf
   141:         state: present
   142:         insertafter: "\\[mysqld\\]"
   143:         line: "max_allowed_packet=1024M"
   144:       when: server_cnf_contents.stdout.find('max_allowed_packet') == -1
   145:       register: server_cnf_packet
   146:     - name: network connection properties

   148:         path: /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf

   152:         line: "{{ item }}"

   155:       loop:

   158:     - name: read client.cnf
   159:       shell: cat /etc/my.cnf.d/mysql-clients.cnf
   160:       register: client_cnf_contents
   161:       changed_when: false
   162:     - name: update client.cnf if needed
   163:       lineinfile:
   164:         path: /etc/my.cnf.d/mysql-clients.cnf
   165:         state: present
   166:         regexp: "^{{ item }}$"
   167:         insertafter: "\\[mysql\\]"
   168:         line: "{{ item }}"
   169:       when: not client_cnf_contents.stdout is match ('^' + item)
   170:       register: client_cnf
   171:       loop:
   172:         - "socket={{ mariadb_data_folder }}/mysql.sock"
   173: 
   174: - name: set data folder
   175:   become: yes
   176:   lineinfile:
   177:     path: /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf
   178:     insertafter: "\\[mysqld\\]"
   179:     regexp: '^datadir='
   180:     line: 'datadir={{ mariadb_data_folder }}'
   181: 
   182: - name: set log folder

   186:     insertafter: "\\[mysqld\\]"
   187:     regexp: '^log-error='
   188:     line: 'log-error={{ mariadb_log_folder }}/mariadb.log'
   189: 
   190: - name: set socket path
   191:   become: yes
   192:   lineinfile:
   193:     path: /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf
   194:     insertafter: "\\[mysqld\\]"
   195:     regexp: '^socket='
   196:     line: 'socket={{ mariadb_data_folder}}/mysql.sock'
   197: 
   198: - name: mariadb logrotate
   199:   become: yes
   200:   template:
   201:     src: logrotate.d/mariadb
   202:     dest: /etc/logrotate.d/mariadb
   203: 
   204: - name: initialize database structures if needed
   205:   become: yes
   206:   become_user: mysql
   207:   command: mysql_install_db
   208:   args:
   209:     chdir: "{{ mariadb_data_folder }}"
   210:     creates: "{{ mariadb_data_folder }}/mysql/"
   211: 
   212: - name: enable MariaDB to start on boot
   213:   become: yes
   214:   systemd:
   215:     daemon_reload: true
   216:     name: mariadb
   217:     enabled: yes
   218:     masked: no

   223:     name: mariadb

     7: # Copied and modified from `file_permissions/ansible.yml` template

     9: # Sets mode 0600 and ownership root:root on all audit config files.
    10: # Installs an auditd.service dropin to restore 0600 on audit.rules after augenrules

    17:     owner: root
    18:     group: root
    19:     state: file
    20:   loop:

    22:     - /etc/audit/auditd.conf

    28:     paths: /etc/audit/rules.d/

   210:     extended: true

   212:   delegate_facts: true

   240:     dest: "{{ hostvars['kubeinit-facts'].local_ssh_dir + '/id_' + hostvars['kubeinit-facts'].ssh_keytype }}"

   248: - name: Generate an OpenSSH keypair for the cluster
   249:   community.crypto.openssh_keypair:
   250:     path: "{{ kubeinit_cluster_keypair_path }}"
   251:     type: "{{ hostvars['kubeinit-facts'].ssh_keytype }}"
   252:     comment: "{{ hostvars['kubeinit-facts'].cluster_name + ' ansible-controller' }}"

   256: - name: Set authorized_key fact from keypair
   257:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   258:     authorized_key: "{{ _result_keypair.public_key + ' ' + _result_keypair.comment }}"
   259: 
   260: - name: Add cluster authorized_key to root account of all hypervisors
   261:   ansible.posix.authorized_key:
   262:     user: root
   263:     key: "{{ authorized_key }}"
   264:     state: present
   265:   become: true
   266:   become_user: root
   267:   loop: "{{ groups['kubeinit_hypervisors'] }}"
   268:   delegate_to: "{{ item }}"
   269:   delegate_facts: true

   286: 
   287: - name: Set kubeinit_cluster_ssh_config fact
   288:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   289:     kubeinit_cluster_ssh_config: "{{ hostvars['kubeinit-facts'].local_ssh_dir + '/' + hostvars['kubeinit-facts'].cluster_name + '_config' }}"

   299:     _param_keypair_path: "{{ kubeinit_cluster_keypair_path }}"
   300:     _param_dest_path: "{{ kubeinit_cluster_ssh_config }}"
   301:     _param_include_paths: "{{ kubeinit_cluster_ssh_include_paths }}"

   305:     remote_user: 'root'
   306:   delegate_to: 'kubeinit-facts'
   307:   delegate_facts: true

   309: - name: Add ansible_ssh_extra_args to hypervisors
   310:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:

   313:   loop: "{{ groups['kubeinit_hypervisors'] }}"
   314:   delegate_to: "{{ item }}"
   315:   delegate_facts: true
   316: 
   317: - name: Confirm that we have ansible host connectivity
   318:   ansible.builtin.ping:
   319:   loop: "{{ groups['kubeinit_hypervisors'] }}"
   320:   delegate_to: "{{ item }}"
   321:   delegate_facts: true

name: Install python and core libraries
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Install a specified version of python. Uses a repository that provides newer
     3: # versions of python, since Ubuntu doesn't (deadsnakes).
     4: # 
     5: # Note that Ubuntu splits up core python libraries into many packages; most are
     6: # required to create the venv. Contents may differ depending on the version of
     7: # python – for example, python3.8-distutils falls back to python3-distutils.
     8: # 
     9: # We include the generic python3-setuptools because it's required to create the
    10: # virtual environment; later we can update pip and setuptools inside it.
    11: 
    12: - name: Add python apt repository
    13:   become: true
    14:   ansible.builtin.apt_repository:
    15:     repo: ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
    16: 
    17: - name: Pin python packages to deadsnakes to avoid rc/alpha versions from distro mirror
    18:   # The Princeton math mirror has a higher apt priority than deadsnakes, causing
    19:   # pre-release builds (e.g. 3.11.0rc1) to be installed instead of the formal
    20:   # release. 3.11.0rc1 lacks sys.get_int_max_str_digits, which torch/kraken
    21:   # import unconditionally, causing a startup crash. This pin ensures deadsnakes
    22:   # always wins. Can be removed if the Princeton mirror is fixed or removed.
    23:   become: true
    24:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    25:     dest: /etc/apt/preferences.d/deadsnakes-python
    26:     content: |
    27:       Package: python{{ python_version }} python{{ python_version }}-* libpython{{ python_version }}*
    28:       Pin: release o=LP-PPA-deadsnakes
    29:       Pin-Priority: 900
    30:     mode: "0644"
    31: 
    32: - name: Install python and core libraries
    33:   become: true
    34:   ansible.builtin.apt:
    35:     name:
    36:       - python3-setuptools
    37:       - python{{ python_version }}
    38:       - python{{ python_version }}-venv
    39:     state: latest
    40:     update_cache: true
    41: 
    42: - name: Install distutils for python < 3.12
    43:   become: true
    44:   ansible.builtin.apt:
    45:     name:
    46:       - python{{ python_version }}-distutils
    47:     state: latest
    48:     update_cache: true
    49:   when: python_version is version('3.12', '<')

source_context:

    24:   when: execution is defined

    28: #---------------------------------------------------
    29: - name: Touch to make sure hostlist exists
    30:   file:
    31:     path: "{{ deploy_working_dir }}/hostlist"
    32:     state: touch
    33:     mode: '0644'
    34: 
    35: #---------------------------------------------------

    37: #---------------------------------------------------
    38: - name: Create EC2 keypair
    39:   ec2_key:
    40:     name: "{{ openshift_cluster_name }}-{{ workshop_prefix }}-key"
    41:     region: "{{ region }}"
    42:     state: "{{ aws_state }}"
    43:   register: ec2_key

    45: - debug:
    46:     var: ec2_key

    49:   copy:
    50:     content: "{{ ec2_key.key.private_key }}\n"
    51:     dest: "{{ ssh_key_path }}"
    52:     mode: 0400
    53:   when: ec2_key.changed
    54: 
    55: - name: Write ssh public key
    56:   openssl_publickey:
    57:     path: "{{ ssh_key_path }}.pub"
    58:     privatekey_path: "{{ ssh_key_path }}"
    59:   when: ec2_key.changed
    60: 
    61: - name: template values in operators
    62:   template:
    63:     src: "sshkey.yaml.j2"
    64:     dest: "{{ openshift_build_path }}/sshkey.yaml"
    65:   when: ec2_key.key.private_key is defined
    66: 
    67: - name: Create OpenShift ssh-key secret
    68:   kubernetes.core.k8s:
    69:     state: present
    70:     src: "{{ openshift_build_path }}/sshkey.yaml"
    71:   when: ec2_key.key.private_key is defined
    72: 
    73: - name: create user sshkey secret template
    74:   template:
    75:     src: "sshkey-user.yaml.j2"
    76:     dest: "{{ openshift_build_path }}/sshkey-user{{ item }}.yaml"
    77:   when: ec2_key.key.private_key is defined
    78:   with_sequence: start=1 count="{{ openshift_user_count }}"
    79:

    83:     src: hosts.j2
    84:     mode: '644'

    96:       workshop_prefix: "{{ workshop_prefix }}"

   107:     state: "{{ aws_state }}"
   108:     tags:
   109:       Name: "{{ openshift_cluster_name }}-{{ workshop_prefix }}-igw"
   110:       username: "{{ local_user }}"
   111:       workshop: "{{ workshop_name }}"
   112:       workshop_prefix: "{{ workshop_prefix }}"

   121:       {% if ports.tcp != None %}

1: ---
     2: 
     3: # Set SSH authentication socket fact on delegated host
     4: 
     5: # Note: Registered results are not delegated to 'delegate_to' hosts, they are
     6: # kept as facts on the current host, so we must throttle setting registered
     7: # result so it is set on correct delegated host (the fact is used later on the
     8: # delegated host).
     9: 
    10: - block:
    11:     - name: Get SSH auth socket on remote machine (so we can forward it to rsync container)
    12:       command: echo "$SSH_AUTH_SOCK"
    13:       register: ssh_auth_sock_result
    14:       delegate_to: "{{ item.dest_host }}"
    15: 
    16:     - name: Set SSH authentication socket on delegated host
    17:       set_fact:
    18:         ssh_auth_sock: "{{ hostvars[inventory_hostname].ssh_auth_sock_result.stdout }}"
    19:       delegate_to: "{{ item.dest_host }}"
    20:       delegate_facts: True
    21:   throttle: 1

    78:     - command: iptables

    11:       - --config

name: Extract ret_code.msg from job with ID {{ job_status_id }}
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: - name: "Query job {{ job_status_id }}"
     3:   ibm.ibm_zos_core.zos_job_query:
     4:     job_name: "*"
     5:     owner: "*"
     6:     job_id: "{{ job_status_id }}"
     7:   register: job_status_query_result
     8:   ignore_errors: true
     9: 
    10: - name: Normalize return values
    11:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    12:     job_status_jobs_list: "{{ job_status_query_result.jobs }}"
    13:   when: job_status_query_result is defined and job_status_query_result.jobs is defined and (job_status_query_result.jobs | length > 0)
    14: 
    15: - name: "Extract ret_code.msg from job with ID {{ job_status_id }}"
    16:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    17:     job_status_code: >-
    18:       {% set rc = job_status_jobs_list[0].ret_code | default({}) %}
    19:       {% if rc is mapping %}
    20:         {% if rc.msg is defined and rc.msg is not none and rc.msg | string != '' %}
    21:           {{ rc.msg | string | trim }}
    22:         {% elif rc.msg_txt is defined and rc.msg_txt is not none and rc.msg_txt | string != '' %}
    23:           {{ rc.msg_txt | string | trim }}
    24:         {% elif rc.message is defined and rc.message is not none and rc.message | string != '' %}
    25:           {{ rc.message | string | trim }}
    26:         {% else %}
    27:           UNKNOWN
    28:         {% endif %}
    29:       {% else %}
    30:         {{ rc | string | trim }}
    31:       {% endif %}
    32:     job_status_is_active: "{{ 'AC' in (job_status_jobs_list[0].ret_code.msg | default('')) }}"
    33: 
    34: - name: Clean job_status_code value
    35:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    36:     job_status_code: "{{ job_status_code | trim }}"
    37: 
    38: - name: "Verify job is found - {{ job_status_id }}"
    39:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    40:     job_status_code: "JOB_NOT_FOUND"
    41:     job_status_is_active: "JOB_NOT_FOUND"
    42:   when: job_status_query_result is failed or job_status_jobs_list is not defined or job_status_jobs_list | length == 0
    43: 
    44: - name: "Display job status and active status from job with id {{ job_status_id }}"
    45:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    46:     msg:
    47:       job_status_code: "{{ job_status_code }}"
    48:       job_status_is_active: "{{ job_status_is_active }}"

    25: - name: Find the pubkeys available in the keys repo

    28:     patterns: "*.pub"

    32:   run_once: true
    33:   register: found_pubkeys

    36: - name: Build the list of users with a pubkey in the keys repo
    37:   set_fact:

    39:       {{
    40:         found_pubkeys.files | default([])
    41:         | map(attribute='path')
    42:         | map('basename')
    43:         | map('regex_replace', '\.pub$', '')
    44:         | list
    45:       }}

    47: # A missing pubkey shouldn't be fatal; the user simply doesn't get access.
    48: # The warning is about the keys repo rather than the host, so emit it once on
    49: # the controller instead of once per user per host.
    50: - name: Warn about users with no pubkey in the keys repo
    51:   debug:
    52:     msg: "WARNING: No pubkey found for '{{ item.name }}' in {{ keys_repo }}; skipping their authorized_keys."
    53:   with_items: "{{ pubkey_users }}"
    54:   # The user dicts carry emails and WireGuard peer info; only log the username
    55:   loop_control:
    56:     label: "{{ item.name }}"
    57:   delegate_to: localhost
    58:   become: false
    59:   run_once: true
    60:   when:
    61:     - keys_repo is defined
    62:     - item.key is undefined
    63:     - item.name not in keys_repo_pubkeys
    64: 
    65: # NOTE: the key has to be a conditional expression rather than
    66: # "item.key | default(lookup(...))" -- Jinja evaluates default()'s argument

    68: # file in the keys repo.
    69: - name: Update authorized_keys
    70:   authorized_key:
    71:     user: "{{ item.name }}"
    72:     key: "{{ item.key if item.key is defined else lookup('file', keys_repo_path + '/ssh/' + item.name + '.pub') }}"

    75:   loop_control:
    76:     label: "{{ item.name }}"

    78:     item.key is defined

1: ---
     2: # Purpose: Reconcile one (fabric, vlan, subnet) triple from `maas_networking`
     3: # against MAAS — create the subnet if missing, otherwise PUT the desired
     4: # gateway_ip / managed flag, then push DNS servers and reconcile IP ranges.
     5: # Called in a loop from networking.yml over every subnet across every VLAN
     6: # across every fabric.
     7: #
     8: # Expects:
     9: #   - trio                  : [fabric_obj, vlan_obj, subnet_obj]
    10: #                             (one element of `_subnet_triples`)
    11: #   - _vlan_index           : { fabric: { vid_str: vlan_obj } } — the parent
    12: #                             VLAN's MAAS id is read from here
    13: #   - _maas_api, maas_auth_header
    14: # Optional:
    15: #   - maas_global_dns_servers : fallback DNS servers when subnet.dns_servers
    16: #                               is empty/unset
    17: #   - maas_overwrite_ipranges : passed through to subnet_range_create
    18: # Returns: nothing.
    19: # Side effects:
    20: #   - GET  /subnets/                          (list)
    21: #   - POST /subnets/                          (create, if missing)
    22: #   - PUT  /subnets/<id>/                     (update gateway/managed)
    23: #   - PUT  /subnets/<id>/                     (set dns_servers, when present)
    24: #   - GET  /ipranges/                         (used by subnet_range_create)
    25: #   - delegates IP-range creation to subnet_range_create.yml.
    26: 
    27: # 0) Validate input triple
    28: - name: Verify triple input
    29:   assert:
    30:     that:
    31:       - trio is defined
    32:       - trio | length == 3
    33:     fail_msg: "subnet_apply.yml expects trio=[fabric, vlan, subnet], got: {{ trio | default('undefined') }}"
    34: 
    35: # 1) Unpack triple
    36: - name: Extract fabric, vlan, and subnet
    37:   set_fact:
    38:     _fname: "{{ trio[0].fabric }}"
    39:     vlan:   "{{ trio[1] }}"
    40:     subnet: "{{ trio[2] }}"
    41: 
    42: # 2) Ensure VLAN exists in index & resolve its numeric id
    43: - name: Ensure VLAN is present in index
    44:   assert:
    45:     that:
    46:       - _vlan_index[_fname] is defined
    47:       - _vlan_index[_fname][vlan.vid | string] is defined
    48:     fail_msg: >-
    49:       VLAN {{ vlan.vid }} not found in index for fabric {{ _fname }}.
    50:       Known vids here: {{ (_vlan_index.get(_fname, {}) | dict2items | map(attribute='key') | list) }}
    51: 
    52: - name: Resolve VLAN object from index
    53:   set_fact:
    54:     _vobj: "{{ _vlan_index[_fname][vlan.vid | string] }}"
    55: 
    56: - name: Extract VLAN numeric id
    57:   set_fact:
    58:     _vid: "{{ _vobj.id }}"
    59: 
    60: # 3) Read subnets (global) and normalize to a list
    61: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
    62:   no_log: true
    63: 
    64: - name: Read subnets (global list)
    65:   uri:
    66:     url: "{{ _maas_api }}/subnets/"
    67:     method: GET
    68:     headers:
    69:       Authorization: "{{ maas_auth_header }}"
    70:       Accept: application/json
    71:     return_content: true
    72:     use_netrc: false
    73:   register: _subnets_resp
    74:   no_log: true
    75: 
    76: - name: Normalize subnets list
    77:   set_fact:
    78:     _subnets_list: >-
    79:       {{
    80:         (_subnets_resp.json.subnets
    81:           if (_subnets_resp.json is mapping and 'subnets' in _subnets_resp.json)
    82:           else (_subnets_resp.json | default([])))
    83:       }}
    84: 
    85: # Find the existing subnet id by CIDR (none if missing)
    86: - name: Extract existing subnet id by CIDR
    87:   set_fact:
    88:     _existing_subnet_id: >-
    89:       {{
    90:         (_subnets_list
    91:           | selectattr('cidr','equalto', subnet.cidr)
    92:           | map(attribute='id') | list | first)
    93:         | default(none)
    94:       }}
    95: 
    96: - name: Decide if subnet already exists
    97:   set_fact:
    98:     _subnet_exists: "{{ _existing_subnet_id is not none and (_existing_subnet_id|string)|length > 0 }}"
    99: 
   100: # Working subnet id variable (may be set later by create)
   101: - set_fact:
   102:     _subnet_id: "{{ _existing_subnet_id }}"
   103: 
   104: # NOTE: _vid (set above as _vobj.id) is the parent VLAN's numeric id used
   105: # below in subnet create/update bodies as the `vlan` form field.
   106: 
   107: # 4) CREATE if missing
   108: - name: Build subnet create body
   109:   set_fact:
   110:     _subnet_create_body: >-
   111:       {{
   112:         {'cidr': subnet.cidr, 'vlan': _vid}
   113:         | combine( (subnet.gateway is defined) | ternary({'gateway_ip': subnet.gateway}, {}), recursive=True )
   114:         | combine( (subnet.managed is defined) | ternary({'managed': subnet.managed|bool}, {}), recursive=True )
   115:       }}

   117: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
   118:   when: not _subnet_exists
   119:   no_log: true

   142:         (
   143:           _existing_subnet_id
   144:           if _subnet_exists
   145:           else (
   146:             _subnet_create_resp.json.id
   147:             if (_subnet_create_resp is defined and _subnet_create_resp.json is defined and _subnet_create_resp.json.id is defined)
   148:             else none
   149:           )
   150:         )
   151:       }}
   152: 
   153: - name: Ensure _subnet_id is set (fallback lookup)
   154:   set_fact:
   155:     _subnet_id: >-
   156:       {{
   157:         _subnet_id
   158:         if (_subnet_id is not none and (_subnet_id|string)|length > 0)

   166: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml

   168:   no_log: true

   170: - name: Re-read subnets (only if _subnet_id still missing)
   171:   uri:
   172:     url: "{{ _maas_api }}/subnets/"
   173:     method: GET
   174:     headers:

   176:       Accept: application/json
   177:     return_content: true
   178:     use_netrc: false

   181:   no_log: true

   183: - name: Normalize subnets list (refetch)
   184:   set_fact:
   185:     _subnets_list: >-
   186:       {{
   187:         (_subnets_resp_refetch.json.subnets
   188:          if (_subnets_resp_refetch is defined and _subnets_resp_refetch.json is mapping and 'subnets' in _subnets_resp_refetch.json)
   189:          else (_subnets_resp_refetch.json | default([])))

   191:   when: _subnets_resp_refetch is defined

   193: - name: Final fallback - derive _subnet_id from refetch
   194:   set_fact:
   195:     _subnet_id: >-
   196:       {{
   197:         _subnet_id
   198:         if (_subnet_id is not none and (_subnet_id|string)|length > 0)
   199:         else (
   200:           (_subnets_list
   201:             | selectattr('cidr','equalto', subnet.cidr)
   202:             | map(attribute='id') | list | first) | default(none)
   203:         )
   204:       }}

   210:       {{
   211:         {'cidr': subnet.cidr, 'vlan': _vid}
   212:         | combine( (subnet.gateway is defined) | ternary({'gateway_ip': subnet.gateway}, {}), recursive=True )
   213:         | combine( (subnet.managed is defined) | ternary({'managed': subnet.managed|bool}, {}), recursive=True )
   214:       }}

   216: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
   217:   when: _subnet_id is not none

   220: - name: Update subnet (if exists)
   221:   uri:
   222:     url: "{{ _maas_api }}/subnets/{{ _subnet_id }}/"
   223:     method: PUT
   224:     headers:
   225:       Authorization: "{{ maas_auth_header }}"
   226:       Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
   227:       Accept: application/json
   228:     body_format: form-urlencoded
   229:     body: "{{ _subnet_update_body }}"
   230:     status_code: [200]
   231:     return_content: true
   232:     use_netrc: false
   233:   when: _subnet_id is not none and (_subnet_id|string)|length > 0
   234:   no_log: true
   235: 
   236: # 6) DNS servers
   237: # DNS servers: prefer subnet.dns_servers[], else maas_global_dns_servers
   238: - name: Choose DNS servers for this subnet
   239:   set_fact:
   240:     _dns_list: "{{ subnet.dns_servers | default(maas_global_dns_servers | default([])) | list }}"
   241: 
   242: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
   243:   when: _dns_list | length > 0 and _subnet_id is not none and (_subnet_id|string)|length > 0
   244:   no_log: true
   245: 
   246: - name: Set DNS servers on subnet
   247:   uri:
   248:     url: "{{ _maas_api }}/subnets/{{ _subnet_id }}/"
   249:     method: PUT
   250:     headers:
   251:       Authorization: "{{ maas_auth_header }}"
   252:       Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
   253:       Accept: application/json
   254:     body_format: form-urlencoded
   255:     body: "{{ {'dns_servers': _dns_list | join(' ')} }}"
   256:     status_code: [200]
   257:     use_netrc: false
   258:   when: _dns_list | length > 0 and _subnet_id is not none and (_subnet_id|string)|length > 0
   259:   no_log: true
   260: 
   261: # 7) IP ranges
   262: # IP ranges (read from top-level /ipranges/, not /subnets/{id}/ipranges/)
   263: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
   264:   when:
   265:     - _subnet_id is not none
   266:     - subnet.ip_ranges is defined
   267:   no_log: true
   268: 
   269: - name: Read all ipranges (we'll filter by subnet)
   270:   uri:
   271:     url: "{{ _maas_api }}/ipranges/"
   272:     method: GET
   273:     headers:
   274:       Authorization: "{{ maas_auth_header }}"
   275:       Accept: application/json
   276:     return_content: true
   277:     use_netrc: false
   278:     status_code: [200]
   279:   register: _all_ranges_resp
   280:   when:
   281:     - _subnet_id is not none
   282:     - subnet.ip_ranges is defined
   283:   no_log: true
   284: 
   285: # Normalize payload so later tasks don’t depend on .json vs .content
   286: - name: Normalize ipranges payload to a list
   287:   set_fact:
   288:     _ipranges_list: >-
   289:       {{
   290:         _all_ranges_resp.json
   291:           if (_all_ranges_resp is defined and _all_ranges_resp.json is defined and _all_ranges_resp.json != '')
   292:           else (_all_ranges_resp.content | from_json)
   293:       }}
   294:   when:
   295:     - _subnet_id is not none
   296:     - subnet.ip_ranges is defined
   297:     - _all_ranges_resp is defined
   298: 
   299: - name: Show _subnet_id and ipranges count
   300:   debug:
   301:     msg:
   302:       - "_subnet_id (int) = {{ _subnet_id | int }}"
   303:       - "ipranges total = {{ (_ipranges_list | default([])) | length }}"
   304:     verbosity: 1
   305:   when:
   306:     - _subnet_id is not none
   307:     - subnet.ip_ranges is defined
   308:     - _ipranges_list is defined
   309: 
   310: - name: Build normalized ipranges list
   311:   set_fact:
   312:     _ipranges_normalized: |
   313:       {% set out = [] %}
   314:       {% for r in (_ipranges_list | default([])) %}
   315:       {%   set sid = ((r.subnet.id if (r.subnet is mapping and 'id' in r.subnet) else r.subnet) | int) %}
   316:       {%   set _ = out.append({
   317:             'id': r.id,
   318:             'type': r.type,
   319:             'start_ip': r.start_ip,
   320:             'end_ip': r.end_ip,
   321:             'computed_subnet_id': sid
   322:           }) %}
   323:       {% endfor %}
   324:       {{ out }}
   325:   when:
   326:     - _subnet_id is not none
   327:     - subnet.ip_ranges is defined
   328:     - _ipranges_list is defined
   329: 
   330: - name: Filter normalized ipranges to this subnet (robust int compare)
   331:   set_fact:
   332:     _subnet_ranges_existing: |
   333:       {% set sid = _subnet_id | int %}
   334:       {% set out = [] %}
   335:       {% for r in (_ipranges_normalized | default([])) %}
   336:       {%   if (r.computed_subnet_id | int) == sid %}
   337:       {%     set _ = out.append(r) %}
   338:       {%   endif %}
   339:       {% endfor %}
   340:       {{ out }}
   341:   when:
   342:     - _subnet_id is not none
   343:     - subnet.ip_ranges is defined
   344:     - _ipranges_normalized is defined
   345: 
   346: - name: Create missing ranges
   347:   vars:
   348:     _exists: >-
   349:       {{
   350:         (_subnet_ranges_existing | default([]))
   351:         | selectattr('type','equalto', ipr.type | default('reserved'))
   352:         | selectattr('start_ip','equalto', ipr.start_ip)
   353:         | selectattr('end_ip','equalto', ipr.end_ip)
   354:         | list | length > 0
   355:       }}
   356:   include_tasks: subnet_range_create.yml
   357:   loop: "{{ subnet.ip_ranges | default([]) }}"
   358:   loop_control:
   359:     loop_var: ipr
   360:     label: "{{ ipr.type }} {{ ipr.start_ip }}-{{ ipr.end_ip }}"
   361:   when:
   362:     - _subnet_id is not none
   363:     - subnet.ip_ranges is defined
   364:     - not _exists

name: Verify INetSim DNS actually answers
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # =============================================================================
     3: # roles/inetsim/tasks/main.yml
     4: # Installs and configures INetSim on the bare metal sandbox host.
     5: #
     6: # INetSim is a network simulation daemon that intercepts DNS, HTTP, HTTPS,
     7: # SMTP, and FTP traffic from guest VMs and returns synthetic responses.
     8: # It runs on the host, bound to the virbr-det bridge gateway IP, so guests
     9: # can reach it but it is not reachable from the internet or management VPN.
    10: #
    11: # Execution order:
    12: #   1. Install the inetsim package (Ubuntu universe repo)
    13: #   2. Create log and report directories
    14: #   3. Deploy inetsim.conf (bind address, services, log paths)
    15: #   4. Install a systemd drop-in that orders INetSim after libvirtd
    16: #      (so the virbr-det bridge IP exists before INetSim tries to bind)
    17: #   5. Enable and start the inetsim service
    18: #
    19: # Dependency on virbr-det:
    20: #   INetSim binds to {{ detonation_gateway }} (the virbr-det bridge IP).
    21: #   This IP only exists after libvirtd starts and brings up the detonation
    22: #   network. The systemd drop-in (step 4) enforces this ordering at boot.
    23: #   During the Ansible run, the networking role runs before this role, so
    24: #   the bridge is already up by the time this role executes.
    25: #
    26: # Author: Christopher Shaiman
    27: # License: Apache 2.0
    28: # =============================================================================
    29: 
    30: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    31: # Install
    32: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    33: 
    34: - name: Install inetsim
    35:   ansible.builtin.apt:
    36:     name: inetsim
    37:     state: present
    38:     update_cache: false
    39:   # inetsim is in Ubuntu universe; ensure universe is enabled before running Ansible.
    40:   # Command if needed: add-apt-repository universe
    41: 
    42: - name: Install dig (used to prove INetSim's DNS actually answers)
    43:   ansible.builtin.apt:
    44:     name: bind9-dnsutils
    45:     state: present
    46:     update_cache: false
    47: 
    48: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    49: # Net::DNS compatibility patch (#464)
    50: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    51: # INetSim 1.3.2 (May 2020, and upstream has not released since) calls the
    52: # historical Net::DNS::Nameserver::main_loop, which is now:
    53: #
    54: #     sub main_loop { carp 'deprecated...'; &start_server; exit; }
    55: #
    56: # and start_server begins:
    57: #
    58: #     my $pid = $$;                                    # FILE-scoped, set at load
    59: #     croak '...in a subprocess' unless $$ == $pid;    # Nameserver.pm:542
    60: #
    61: # $pid is captured when the module is compiled — in INetSim's parent. INetSim
    62: # forks a child per service, so the DNS child always fails that test, croaks,
    63: # and exits 25. It had logged "started" one line earlier and never logs
    64: # "stopped"; its stderr is not wired to the journal. The result is a service
    65: # that reports itself up and has never answered a single query, which is why
    66: # every analysis recorded `answers: []` (#456).
    67: #
    68: # loop_once is the other historical entry point: it does not call start_server,
    69: # carries no pid guard, and creates its own sockets lazily. Verified on the host
    70: # by replicating INetSim's structure (module loaded in parent, fork, child runs
    71: # loop_once): the child survived, bound udp/5300, and answered a query with the
    72: # gateway address.
    73: #
    74: # This edits a distro-owned file, so it is written to be self-healing: `replace`
    75: # re-applies after any apt upgrade that restores the original, and the assertion
    76: # below fails the deploy if the anchor ever stops matching. Neither is the real
    77: # guard — that is the live query at the end of this file, because a file that
    78: # looks right is not a DNS server that answers.
    79: 
    80: # DNS.pm is ISO-8859, not UTF-8: one byte, 0xfc, the 'ü' in the German comment
    81: # "IP-Adressen für MX in Additional Section". ansible.builtin.replace and
    82: # lineinfile both decode the whole file as UTF-8 and abort:
    83: #
    84: #   'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xfc in position 7746: invalid start byte
    85: #
    86: # sed edits bytes, so it does not care. LC_ALL=C keeps it that way — under a
    87: # UTF-8 locale, GNU tools can treat a file with an invalid sequence as binary
    88: # and quietly decline to match.
    89: 
    90: - name: Patch INetSim DNS to use loop_once instead of main_loop (#464)
    91:   ansible.builtin.shell:
    92:     cmd: |
    93:       set -eu
    94:       export LC_ALL=C
    95:       f=/usr/share/perl5/INetSim/DNS.pm
    96:       if grep -qF 'loop_once(10)' "$f"; then
    97:           echo unchanged
    98:           exit 0
    99:       fi
   100:       # Only reached when unpatched, so the backup is always of a pristine file
   101:       # — including after an apt upgrade restores the original.
   102:       cp -a "$f" "$f.lamware.bak"
   103:       # '#' is the s/// delimiter here because ansible-lint's risky-shell-pipe
   104:       # heuristic reads a vertical bar anywhere in a shell task as a pipeline
   105:       # and demands pipefail — misleading to add to a task with no pipe in it.
   106:       sed -i 's#^\([[:space:]]*\)\$server->main_loop;[[:space:]]*$#\1while (1) { $server->loop_once(10); }#' "$f"
   107:       # sed exits 0 when its pattern matches nothing. That silent no-op is the
   108:       # entire failure mode this task exists to avoid, so confirm the edit.
   109:       grep -qF 'loop_once(10)' "$f"
   110:       echo patched
   111:     executable: /bin/bash
   112:   register: inetsim_dns_patch
   113:   changed_when: inetsim_dns_patch.stdout is search('patched')
   114:   notify: Restart inetsim
   115: 
   116: - name: Assert the DNS patch applied (a silent no-op here is the whole failure mode)
   117:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   118:     cmd: |
   119:       set -eu
   120:       export LC_ALL=C
   121:       f=/usr/share/perl5/INetSim/DNS.pm
   122:       # Present in its patched form...
   123:       grep -qF 'loop_once(10)' "$f"
   124:       # ...and the croaking call is gone.
   125:       ! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*\$server->main_loop;' "$f"
   126:     executable: /bin/bash
   127:   changed_when: false
   128: 
   129: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   130: # Log and report directories
   131: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   132: 
   133: - name: Create inetsim log directory
   134:   ansible.builtin.file:
   135:     path: "{{ inetsim_log_dir }}"
   136:     state: directory
   137:     owner: inetsim
   138:     group: inetsim
   139:     mode: "0750"
   140: 
   141: - name: Create inetsim report directory
   142:   ansible.builtin.file:
   143:     path: "{{ inetsim_report_dir }}"
   144:     state: directory
   145:     owner: inetsim
   146:     group: inetsim
   147:     mode: "0750"
   148: 
   149: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   150: # Configuration
   151: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   152: 
   153: - name: Deploy inetsim.conf
   154:   ansible.builtin.template:
   155:     src: inetsim.conf.j2
   156:     dest: /etc/inetsim/inetsim.conf
   157:     owner: root
   158:     group: inetsim
   159:     mode: "0640"
   160:   notify: Restart inetsim
   161: 
   162: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   163: # Systemd drop-in — order INetSim after libvirtd
   164: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   165: # INetSim binds to the virbr-det bridge gateway IP. That IP only exists
   166: # after libvirtd starts and activates the detonation network. Without this
   167: # ordering, INetSim starts at boot before the bridge is up and fails to bind,
   168: # leaving guests with no network simulation until the service is manually restarted.
   169: 
   170: - name: Create systemd drop-in directory for inetsim
   171:   ansible.builtin.file:
   172:     path: /etc/systemd/system/inetsim.service.d
   173:     state: directory
   174:     owner: root
   175:     group: root
   176:     mode: "0755"
   177: 
   178: - name: Install inetsim systemd drop-in (require libvirtd)
   179:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   180:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/inetsim.service.d/after-libvirtd.conf
   181:     owner: root
   182:     group: root
   183:     mode: "0644"
   184:     content: |
   185:       # Ansible-managed: ensure virbr-det bridge IP exists before INetSim binds.
   186:       # libvirtd brings up the detonation network (and its gateway IP) at startup.
   187:       [Unit]
   188:       Requires=libvirtd.service
   189:       After=libvirtd.service
   190:   notify:
   191:     - Reload systemd daemon
   192:     - Restart inetsim
   193: 
   194: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   195: # Enable and start
   196: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   197: 
   198: # The unit is generated from a SysV script whose `stop` kills only the PID in
   199: # the pidfile and never removes it (init script line 81: `#rm -f $PIDFILE`).
   200: # When the main process dies without cleanup the pidfile outlives it, the
   201: # service children keep their ports, and every later start is a no-op that
   202: # reports success. Observed here: the unit read `inactive` for 19 days while
   203: # four children served traffic, and the #459 deploy could not restart over it.
   204: # Full supervision fix is #463; this clears the specific state that makes a
   205: # restart silently do nothing.
   206: 
   207: - name: Clear a wedged INetSim (stale pidfile, orphaned service children)
   208:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   209:     cmd: |
   210:       pid=$(cat /var/run/inetsim.pid 2>/dev/null || true)
   211:       if [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
   212:           echo healthy
   213:           exit 0
   214:       fi
   215:       rm -f /var/run/inetsim.pid
   216:       pkill -f '^inetsim_' 2>/dev/null || true
   217:       echo cleaned
   218:   register: inetsim_wedge
   219:   changed_when: inetsim_wedge.stdout is search('cleaned')
   220: 
   221: - name: Enable and start inetsim service
   222:   ansible.builtin.systemd:
   223:     name: inetsim
   224:     state: started
   225:     enabled: true
   226:     daemon_reload: true
   227: 
   228: - name: Flush handlers so the check below tests the restarted service
   229:   ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
   230: 
   231: # The guard that matters. `systemctl is-active` was wrong in both directions on
   232: # this host — `inactive` while four children served traffic, then `active` with
   233: # no DNS at all — and a config file with the right port in it proves nothing.
   234: # Ask the question the rest of the platform depends on: does a query get an
   235: # answer? This is the check that would have caught #456 on day one.
   236: 
   237: - name: Verify INetSim DNS actually answers
   238:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   239:     cmd: >-
   240:       set -o pipefail;
   241:       dig +short +tries=1 +time=3 -p {{ inetsim_dns_port }}
   242:       @{{ detonation_gateway }} inetsim-deploy-probe.invalid
   243:       | grep -Eo '^[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}$' | head -1

    47:     login_password: "{{ mongo_admin_pw }}"

name: Check whether tailscale is installed
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Real sshd on an alternate port, alongside Tailscale SSH.
     3: #
     4: # On a host running Tailscale SSH (the "SSH" badge in the admin console; RunSSH=true),
     5: # tailscaled intercepts every TAILNET connection to port 22 and answers with Tailscale's
     6: # own SSH server — `ssh -vv` reports `remote software version Tailscale`. That server
     7: # authenticates by tailnet identity + ACL (check mode = the browser prompt) and never
     8: # consults authorized_keys, so key-based automation (the rustd.xyz panel's SFTP map
     9: # fetch, rustd.xyz#385) cannot reach the real sshd over the tailnet at all. LAN
    10: # connections are untouched, which is why the problem only shows from cloud hosts.
    11: #
    12: # Interception is port-22-only (verified live on ubuntu-cube 2026-08-13: the game port
    13: # passed through to the host while :22 answered as Tailscale). So the fix that keeps
    14: # BOTH security properties — check-mode for humans on 22, key-only auth for automation —
    15: # is the real sshd listening on a second port:
    16: #
    17: #   tailnet :22   -> Tailscale SSH (humans; browser check per the tailnet ACL)
    18: #   tailnet :2222 -> OpenSSH (key auth; a compromised peer node without the key gets nothing)
    19: #   LAN :22       -> OpenSSH, unchanged; the alternate port is a NEW listener on the LAN
    20: #                    too (all interfaces) — harmless behind the router, but not "no change"
    21: #
    22: # Applied to every Ubuntu host with tailscale installed rather than only those with
    23: # RunSSH currently on: it is harmless where Tailscale SSH is off, and enabling the badge
    24: # later must not silently strand automation.
    25: 
    26: - name: Check whether tailscale is installed
    27:   ansible.builtin.stat:
    28:     path: /usr/bin/tailscale
    29:   register: sshd_alt_port_tailscale
    30: 
    31: - name: Configure the alternate sshd port
    32:   when:
    33:     - ansible_facts['distribution'] == 'Ubuntu'
    34:     - sshd_alt_port_tailscale.stat.exists
    35:   become: true
    36:   block:
    37:     # Ubuntu 22.10+ runs sshd socket-activated: ssh.socket owns the listen ports and
    38:     # `Port` lines in sshd_config are silently ignored. Which mechanism is live decides
    39:     # where the alternate port must be declared. Enablement is the wants-symlink that
    40:     # `systemctl is-enabled` itself checks — stat'ing it avoids shelling out.
    41:     - name: Check whether ssh.socket activation is in use
    42:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    43:         path: /etc/systemd/system/sockets.target.wants/ssh.socket
    44:       register: sshd_alt_port_socket_state
    45: 
    46:     - name: Add the alternate port to ssh.socket (socket-activated hosts)
    47:       when: sshd_alt_port_socket_state.stat.exists
    48:       block:
    49:         - name: Create the ssh.socket override directory
    50:           ansible.builtin.file:
    51:             path: /etc/systemd/system/ssh.socket.d
    52:             state: directory
    53:             owner: root
    54:             group: root
    55:             mode: "0755"
    56: 
    57:         # ListenStream entries are ADDITIVE: the stock unit keeps 22, this adds the
    58:         # alternate. (An empty `ListenStream=` line would reset instead — do not add one.)
    59:         #
    60:         # BOTH address families, explicitly, like the stock unit's `0.0.0.0:22` + `[::]:22`
    61:         # pair: a bare `ListenStream={{ sshd_alt_port_number }}` bound ONLY `[::]` and that
    62:         # socket turned out v6-only in the field — IPv4 to the port was refused even on
    63:         # loopback, which is precisely the address family the tailnet fetch uses
    64:         # (found live on ubuntu-cube, 2026-08-13).
    65:         - name: Add the alternate port to ssh.socket
    66:           ansible.builtin.copy:
    67:             dest: /etc/systemd/system/ssh.socket.d/alt-port.conf
    68:             content: |
    69:               # Managed by ansible (sshd_alt_port). See the role for why this exists.
    70:               [Socket]
    71:               ListenStream=0.0.0.0:{{ sshd_alt_port_number }}
    72:               ListenStream=[::]:{{ sshd_alt_port_number }}
    73:             owner: root
    74:             group: root
    75:             mode: "0644"
    76:           notify: Restart ssh.socket
    77: 
    78:     - name: Add the alternate port via sshd_config (service-activated hosts)
    79:       when: not sshd_alt_port_socket_state.stat.exists
    80:       block:
    81:         # Both Port lines are needed together: once any Port is specified, sshd stops
    82:         # defaulting to 22.
    83:         - name: Add the alternate port to sshd_config.d
    84:           ansible.builtin.copy:
    85:             dest: /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-alt-port.conf
    86:             content: |
    87:               # Managed by ansible (sshd_alt_port). See the role for why this exists.
    88:               Port 22
    89:               Port {{ sshd_alt_port_number }}
    90:             owner: root
    91:             group: root
    92:             mode: "0644"
    93:             validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
    94:           notify: Restart ssh

   243:     mode: "0644"
   244:   loop: "{{ ollama_modelfiles }}"
   245:   loop_control:
   246:     label: "{{ item.name }}"
   247:   when: ollama_modelfiles | length > 0
   248:   tags:
   249:     - ollama
   250:     - modelfiles
   251: 
   252: - name: Create Modelfile variants when absent
   253:   become: true
   254:   ansible.builtin.shell: >
   255:     docker exec -i {{ ollama_container_name | quote }}
   256:     ollama create {{ item.name | quote }} -f /dev/stdin
   257:     < {{ (ollama_data_path ~ '/modelfiles/'
   258:           ~ (item.name | regex_replace('[^A-Za-z0-9]', '_'))
   259:           ~ '.Modelfile') | quote }}
   260:   loop: "{{ ollama_modelfiles }}"
   261:   loop_control:
   262:     label: "{{ item.name }}"
   263:   when:
   264:     - ollama_modelfiles | length > 0
   265:     - item.name not in ollama_installed_tags.stdout
   266:   changed_when: true # Only runs when variant missing (per `when:`); success == change
   267:   tags:
   268:     - ollama
   269:     - modelfiles
   270: 
   271: # Display connection info

   273:   ansible.builtin.debug:

   279:

   283:       Large models (70B+) will use GPU + RAM offloading automatically.
   284: 
   285:       To use from Hermes Agent (see roles/hermes), the OpenAI-compatible
   286:       endpoint is: http://{{ inventory_hostname }}:{{ ollama_port }}/v1
   287:   tags:
   288:     - ollama
   289:     - info

name: Set the root filesystem fact
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # =============================================================================
     3: # Dedicated Docker data disk
     4: # =============================================================================
     5: # The CI guests carry a second block device for /var/lib/docker. Without it the
     6: # image and build cache share the boot filesystem and fill it, and every job on
     7: # the host then fails with ENOSPC regardless of what it was testing.
     8: #
     9: # The device is addressed by its /dev/disk/by-id path. Kernel names (/dev/sdb)
    10: # are assigned in discovery order and are not stable across reboots — a mkfs
    11: # against the wrong one destroys the boot disk.
    12: #
    13: # The filesystem is written to the whole device, with no partition table. A
    14: # single-purpose data disk gains nothing from one, and it makes "does this
    15: # device already carry something" a single blkid question instead of a
    16: # partition-table-plus-partition walk.
    17: 
    18: - name: Validate the Docker data device is declared
    19:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    20:     that:
    21:       - github_runner_data_device is defined
    22:       - github_runner_data_device | length > 0
    23:       - github_runner_data_device is match('^/dev/disk/by-(id|uuid|path)/')
    24:     fail_msg: >-
    25:       github_runner_data_device must name this guest's Docker data disk by a
    26:       stable /dev/disk/by-id (or by-uuid, by-path) path. Kernel names are not
    27:       stable across reboots.
    28: 
    29: - name: Resolve the Docker data device
    30:   ansible.builtin.stat:
    31:     path: "{{ github_runner_data_device }}"
    32:     follow: true
    33:   register: github_runner_data_dev
    34: 
    35: - name: Assert the Docker data device is present
    36:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    37:     that:
    38:       - github_runner_data_dev.stat.exists
    39:       - github_runner_data_dev.stat.isblk
    40:     fail_msg: >-
    41:       {{ github_runner_data_device }} does not resolve to a block device on
    42:       this host. Attach the data disk to the guest before converging; nothing
    43:       here formats a device it cannot identify.
    44: 
    45: - name: Read existing signatures on the Docker data device
    46:   ansible.builtin.command:
    47:     cmd: "blkid -p -o export {{ github_runner_data_device }}"
    48:   register: github_runner_data_blkid
    49:   changed_when: false
    50:   # blkid exits 2 when it finds no signature at all — the expected state for a
    51:   # never-used disk. Any other non-zero is a real error.
    52:   failed_when: github_runner_data_blkid.rc not in [0, 2]
    53: 
    54: - name: Refuse to format a device that already carries data
    55:   vars:
    56:     _signatures: "{{ github_runner_data_blkid.stdout | default('') }}"
    57:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    58:     that:
    59:       - _signatures is not search('^PTTYPE=', multiline=True)
    60:       - >-
    61:         _signatures is not search('^TYPE=', multiline=True)
    62:         or _signatures is search('^TYPE=' ~ github_runner_data_fstype ~ '$',
    63:         multiline=True)
    64:     fail_msg: >-
    65:       {{ github_runner_data_device }} already carries a partition table, or a
    66:       filesystem that is not {{ github_runner_data_fstype }}. Refusing to touch
    67:       it. Signatures found: {{ github_runner_data_blkid.stdout_lines | default([]) | join(' ') }}
    68: 
    69: - name: Create the Docker data filesystem
    70:   community.general.filesystem:
    71:     dev: "{{ github_runner_data_device }}"
    72:     fstype: "{{ github_runner_data_fstype }}"
    73:     # `force` is deliberately absent. The module is a no-op when the requested
    74:     # filesystem is already present, and errors rather than overwriting a
    75:     # different one.
    76: 
    77: - name: Read the Docker data filesystem UUID
    78:   ansible.builtin.command:
    79:     cmd: "blkid -s UUID -o value {{ github_runner_data_device }}"
    80:   register: github_runner_data_uuid
    81:   changed_when: false
    82: 
    83: - name: Check whether /var/lib/docker already has its own filesystem
    84:   ansible.builtin.command:
    85:     cmd: findmnt -no SOURCE /var/lib/docker
    86:   register: github_runner_docker_mount
    87:   changed_when: false
    88:   failed_when: false
    89: 
    90: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    91: # One-shot migration of an existing /var/lib/docker off the boot disk.
    92: #
    93: # WHY A MOUNT AT /var/lib/docker RATHER THAN Docker's `data-root`:
    94: # the mount leaves Docker's own configuration at its default, so exactly one
    95: # thing has to survive a rebuild — the fstab entry. `data-root` needs BOTH a
    96: # daemon.json that survives and the mount that backs it, and the docker_engine
    97: # role here only writes daemon.json when a flag is set, so a data-root would
    98: # have to take ownership of that file away from it. One thing to survive
    99: # instead of two is the more honest choice, and the converge-time assertion
   100: # below catches either one regressing.
   101: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   102: 
   103: - name: Migrate an existing /var/lib/docker onto the data disk
   104:   when: github_runner_docker_mount.rc != 0
   105:   block:
   106:     - name: Stop Docker for the data-disk migration
   107:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   108:         name: "{{ item }}"
   109:         state: stopped
   110:       loop:
   111:         - docker.service
   112:         - docker.socket
   113: 
   114:     - name: Mount the data filesystem at a staging path
   115:       ansible.posix.mount:
   116:         path: /mnt/docker-data
   117:         src: "UUID={{ github_runner_data_uuid.stdout }}"
   118:         fstype: "{{ github_runner_data_fstype }}"
   119:         state: ephemeral
   120: 
   121:     - name: Copy the existing Docker tree onto the data disk
   122:       ansible.builtin.command:
   123:         cmd: cp -a /var/lib/docker/. /mnt/docker-data/
   124:         creates: /mnt/docker-data/image
   125: 
   126:     - name: Unmount the staging path
   127:       ansible.posix.mount:
   128:         path: /mnt/docker-data
   129:         state: absent
   130: 
   131:     - name: Set the pre-migration tree aside
   132:       ansible.builtin.command:
   133:         cmd: mv /var/lib/docker /var/lib/docker.pre-datadisk
   134:         creates: /var/lib/docker.pre-datadisk
   135: 
   136: - name: Mount the Docker data disk at /var/lib/docker
   137:   ansible.posix.mount:
   138:     path: /var/lib/docker
   139:     src: "UUID={{ github_runner_data_uuid.stdout }}"
   140:     fstype: "{{ github_runner_data_fstype }}"
   141:     opts: defaults
   142:     state: mounted
   143: 
   144: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   145: # containerd's own root, which is NOT under Docker's.
   146: #
   147: # Modern Docker defaults to the containerd snapshotter
   148: # (`driver-type: io.containerd.snapshotter.v1`). Under it, image layers and
   149: # every container's writable layer live in /var/lib/containerd, NOT in
   150: # /var/lib/docker — so mounting the data disk at /var/lib/docker moves almost
   151: # nothing. Observed on two guests: a dedicated 100G data disk sat at 935M / 1%
   152: # used while 90G of snapshots filled the 99G boot disk and took the host down,
   153: # with the old guard passing the whole time because the mount it checked was
   154: # real and correct.
   155: #
   156: # Bind-mounting it into the data disk keeps the "one filesystem, addressed by a
   157: # surviving fstab entry" shape the block above chose deliberately, and works
   158: # whichever snapshotter is active.
   159: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   160: 
   161: - name: Read the filesystem backing /
   162:   ansible.builtin.command:
   163:     cmd: findmnt -no SOURCE --target /
   164:   register: github_runner_root_fs
   165:   changed_when: false
   166: 
   167: - name: Set the root filesystem fact
   168:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   169:     github_runner_fs_root_source: "{{ github_runner_root_fs.stdout | trim }}"
   170: 
   171: - name: Create the containerd directory on the data disk
   172:   ansible.builtin.file:
   173:     path: /var/lib/docker/containerd
   174:     state: directory
   175:     owner: root
   176:     group: root
   177:     mode: "0711"
   178: 
   179: - name: Check whether /var/lib/containerd is already redirected
   180:   ansible.builtin.command:
   181:     cmd: findmnt -no SOURCE --target /var/lib/containerd
   182:   register: github_runner_containerd_mount
   183:   changed_when: false
   184:   failed_when: false
   185: 
   186: - name: Migrate an existing /var/lib/containerd onto the data disk
   187:   when: >-
   188:     github_runner_containerd_mount.stdout | trim
   189:     == github_runner_fs_root_source | default('', true) | trim
   190:     or github_runner_containerd_mount.rc != 0
   191:   block:
   192:     - name: Stop Docker and containerd for the migration
   193:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   194:         name: "{{ item }}"
   195:         state: stopped
   196:       loop:
   197:         - docker.service
   198:         - docker.socket
   199:         - containerd.service
   200: 
   201:     - name: Copy the existing containerd tree onto the data disk
   202:       ansible.builtin.command:
   203:         cmd: cp -a /var/lib/containerd/. /var/lib/docker/containerd/
   204:       register: github_runner_containerd_copy
   205:       changed_when: true
   206:       # An empty or absent source is the fresh-guest case, not a failure.
   207:       failed_when: >-
   208:         github_runner_containerd_copy.rc != 0
   209:         and 'No such file or directory' not in github_runner_containerd_copy.stderr
   210: 
   211:     - name: Set the pre-migration containerd tree aside
   212:       ansible.builtin.command:
   213:         cmd: mv /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/containerd.pre-datadisk
   214:         creates: /var/lib/containerd.pre-datadisk
   215: 
   216:     - name: Recreate the containerd mount point
   217:       ansible.builtin.file:
   218:         path: /var/lib/containerd
   219:         state: directory
   220:         owner: root
   221:         group: root
   222:         mode: "0711"
   223: 
   224: - name: Bind /var/lib/containerd onto the data disk
   225:   ansible.posix.mount:
   226:     path: /var/lib/containerd
   227:     src: /var/lib/docker/containerd
   228:     fstype: none
   229:     opts: bind
   230:     state: mounted
   231: 
   232: - name: Ensure Docker and containerd are running on the data disk
   233:   ansible.builtin.systemd:
   234:     name: "{{ item }}"
   235:     state: started
   236:     enabled: true
   237:   loop:
   238:     - containerd
   239:     - docker
   240: 
   241: # =============================================================================
   242: # Converge-time guard
   243: # =============================================================================
   244: # This runs on EVERY converge, not only during the migration. Without it the
   245: # change regresses silently on the next rebuild, and the only symptom is an
   246: # ENOSPC failure in an unrelated job.
   247: 
   248: - name: Read the filesystems backing / and every Docker data path
   249:   ansible.builtin.command:
   250:     cmd: "findmnt -no SOURCE --target {{ item }}"
   251:   loop: "{{ ['/'] + github_runner_data_paths }}"
   252:   register: github_runner_fs_sources
   253:   changed_when: false
   254: 
   255: - name: Assert no Docker data path is on the root filesystem
   256:   vars:
   257:     _root_fs: "{{ github_runner_fs_sources.results[0].stdout | trim }}"
   258:     _offenders: >-
   259:       {{ github_runner_fs_sources.results[1:]
   260:          | selectattr('stdout', 'search', '^' ~ _root_fs ~ '$')
   261:          | map(attribute='item') | list }}
   262:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   263:     that:
   264:       - _offenders | length == 0
   265:     fail_msg: >-
   266:       {{ _offenders | join(', ') }} {{ 'is' if _offenders | length == 1 else 'are' }}
   267:       on the root filesystem ({{ _root_fs }}). Docker's image and container data
   268:       will fill the boot disk and every job on this runner will fail with ENOSPC
   269:       — as will anything else on the guest, including sshd. Check the fstab
   270:       entries for {{ github_runner_data_paths | join(' and ') }}.
   271:     success_msg: >-
   272:       Every Docker data path ({{ github_runner_data_paths | join(', ') }}) is
   273:       off the root filesystem ({{ _root_fs }}).
   274: 
   275: # The mount above proves where the directories live. It does not prove Docker
   276: # is USING them: `data-root` in a daemon.json, or a storage driver whose data
   277: # lives somewhere else entirely, both move the bytes without moving the mount.
   278: # Ask the daemon directly.
   279: - name: Read Docker's own data root
   280:   ansible.builtin.command:
   281:     cmd: docker info --format '{{ "{{" }}.DockerRootDir{{ "}}" }}'
   282:   register: github_runner_docker_root
   283:   changed_when: false
   284: 
   285: - name: Assert Docker's reported data root is a path this role placed off the boot disk
   286:   vars:
   287:     _reported: "{{ github_runner_docker_root.stdout | trim }}"
   288:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   289:     that:
   290:       - _reported is search('^' ~ (github_runner_data_paths | first))
   291:     fail_msg: >-
   292:       Docker reports its data root as {{ _reported }}, which is not
   293:       {{ github_runner_data_paths | first }}. The mounts this role manages are
   294:       then guarding a directory the daemon does not write to, and the boot disk
   295:       will fill anyway. A daemon.json `data-root` is the usual cause.
   296: 
   297: # Reclaim the boot disk only once the mounts are proven, never before. Either
   298: # migration can happen without the other: a guest converged before the
   299: # containerd bind mount existed already has /var/lib/docker on the data disk.
   300: - name: Reclaim the boot disk after a successful migration
   301:   when: >-
   302:     github_runner_docker_mount.rc != 0
   303:     or github_runner_containerd_mount.rc != 0
   304:   block:
   305:     - name: Remove the pre-migration trees from the boot disk
   306:       ansible.builtin.file:
   307:         path: "{{ item }}"
   308:         state: absent
   309:       loop:
   310:         - /var/lib/docker.pre-datadisk
   311:         - /var/lib/containerd.pre-datadisk
   312: 
   313:     - name: Prune dangling Docker data
   314:       ansible.builtin.command:
   315:         cmd: docker system prune --force
   316:       register: github_runner_prune
   317:       changed_when: "'Total reclaimed space: 0B' not in github_runner_prune.stdout"
