name: Render blackbox exporter configuration
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # prometheus_stack — Prometheus + blackbox_exporter as ONE Docker-in-LXC compose
     3: # stack. One Docker bootstrap, one compose project, two services. Both run on host
     4: # networking: blackbox needs it for ICMP source-routing + NET_RAW, Prometheus to
     5: # reach exporters across VLANs and scrape blackbox on 127.0.0.1.
     6: #
     7: # daemon.json is intentionally NOT written here. The registry-mirror play in
     8: # site.yml is the single owner of /etc/docker/daemon.json on docker LXCs (it sets
     9: # storage-driver + registry mirror together). A per-role write would clobber the
    10: # mirror — see the "single owner" note in site.yml.
    11: 
    12: # Docker itself (docker-ce + compose plugin, LXC-conditional fuse-overlayfs) is
    13: # installed by the docker_engine meta dependency (meta/main.yml). No daemon.json
    14: # (see above) and no venv: the stack deploys via docker_compose_v2, which uses the
    15: # docker compose CLI (not the docker SDK), so compose runs under the system
    16: # interpreter.
    17: 
    18: # =============================================================================
    19: # Config + compose (single project, two services)
    20: # =============================================================================
    21: 
    22: - name: Create prometheus stack data directory
    23:   ansible.builtin.file:
    24:     path: "{{ prometheus_stack_data_dir }}"
    25:     state: directory
    26:     owner: root
    27:     group: root
    28:     mode: "0755"
    29: 
    30: - name: Render prometheus.yml scrape configuration
    31:   ansible.builtin.template:
    32:     src: prometheus.yml.j2
    33:     dest: "{{ prometheus_stack_data_dir }}/prometheus.yml"
    34:     owner: root
    35:     group: root
    36:     mode: "0644"
    37:     unsafe_writes: true
    38:   notify: Reload prometheus config
    39: 
    40: - name: Render blackbox exporter configuration
    41:   ansible.builtin.template:
    42:     src: blackbox.yml.j2
    43:     dest: "{{ prometheus_stack_data_dir }}/blackbox.yml"
    44:     owner: root
    45:     group: root
    46:     mode: "0644"
    47:   notify: Restart prometheus stack
    48: 
    49: - name: Deploy prometheus stack docker-compose template
    50:   ansible.builtin.template:
    51:     src: docker-compose.yml.j2
    52:     dest: "{{ prometheus_stack_data_dir }}/docker-compose.yml"
    53:     owner: root
    54:     group: root
    55:     mode: "0644"
    56:   notify: Restart prometheus stack
    57: 
    58: - name: Deploy and verify the prometheus stack
    59:   block:
    60:     # One-time migration: the previous design ran blackbox-exporter as its own
    61:     # compose project. Tear it down so its fixed container_name is free for the
    62:     # merged project to recreate.
    63:     - name: Check for the legacy standalone blackbox compose project
    64:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    65:         path: "{{ prometheus_stack_legacy_blackbox_dir }}/docker-compose.yml"
    66:       register: prometheus_stack_legacy_blackbox
    67: 
    68:     - name: Tear down the legacy standalone blackbox compose project
    69:       community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
    70:         project_src: "{{ prometheus_stack_legacy_blackbox_dir }}"
    71:         state: absent
    72:       when: prometheus_stack_legacy_blackbox.stat.exists
    73: 
    74:     - name: Remove the legacy standalone blackbox project directory
    75:       ansible.builtin.file:
    76:         path: "{{ prometheus_stack_legacy_blackbox_dir }}"
    77:         state: absent
    78:       when: prometheus_stack_legacy_blackbox.stat.exists
    79: 
    80:     - name: Deploy the prometheus stack via docker compose
    81:       community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
    82:         project_src: "{{ prometheus_stack_data_dir }}"
    83:         state: present
    84: 
    85:     # =========================================================================
    86:     # Health checks — prove BOTH containers run, both serve, the exporter
    87:     # actually completes a probe, AND Prometheus has scraped probe_success into
    88:     # the TSDB (the full pipeline, not just "containers up").
    89:     # =========================================================================
    90:     - name: Verify both stack containers are running
    91:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
    92:         docker ps -q --filter name={{ item }} --filter status=running
    93:       register: prometheus_stack_running
    94:       changed_when: false
    95:       retries: 6
    96:       delay: 5
    97:       until: prometheus_stack_running.stdout != ''
    98:       loop:
    99:         - "{{ prometheus_stack_container_name }}"
   100:         - "{{ prometheus_stack_blackbox_container_name }}"
   101: 
   102:     - name: Verify prometheus is healthy and ready
   103:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   104:         url: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ prometheus_stack_port }}/-/ready"
   105:         status_code: 200
   106:       register: prometheus_stack_ready
   107:       retries: 12
   108:       delay: 5
   109:       until: prometheus_stack_ready.status | default(0) == 200
   110:       changed_when: false
   111: 
   112:     - name: Verify the blackbox exporter answers /-/healthy
   113:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   114:         url: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ prometheus_stack_blackbox_port }}/-/healthy"
   115:         status_code: 200
   116:       register: prometheus_stack_bb_healthy
   117:       retries: 6
   118:       delay: 5
   119:       until: prometheus_stack_bb_healthy.status | default(0) == 200
   120:       changed_when: false
   121: 
   122:     # Real probe: the exporter must run a module and emit metrics, not just answer
   123:     # its own health endpoint. A broken module config or missing NET_RAW fails here.
   124:     - name: Verify the blackbox exporter completes an ICMP probe
   125:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   126:         url: >-
   127:           http://{{ prometheus_stack_blackbox_address }}/probe?target={{ prometheus_stack_smoke_target }}&module=icmp
   128:         return_content: true
   129:         status_code: 200
   130:       register: prometheus_stack_probe
   131:       retries: 6
   132:       delay: 5
   133:       until: "'probe_success' in (prometheus_stack_probe.content | default(''))"
   134:       changed_when: false
   135: 
   136:     # End-to-end: Prometheus must have scraped the exporter and stored
   137:     # probe_success. Exercises scrape + relabel + TSDB, not just service liveness.
   138:     - name: Verify Prometheus has scraped probe_success into the TSDB
   139:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   140:         url: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ prometheus_stack_port }}/api/v1/query?query=probe_success"
   141:         status_code: 200
   142:       register: prometheus_stack_query
   143:       retries: 12
   144:       delay: 5
   145:       until: (prometheus_stack_query.json.data.result | default([]) | length) > 0
   146:       changed_when: false
   147: 
   148:   rescue:
   149:     - name: Capture stack diagnostics on failure
   150:       ansible.builtin.command: "{{ item }}"
   151:       loop:
   152:         - "docker ps -a"
   153:         - "docker logs --tail 50 {{ prometheus_stack_container_name }}"
   154:         - "docker logs --tail 50 {{ prometheus_stack_blackbox_container_name }}"
   155:       register: prometheus_stack_diag
   156:       changed_when: false
   157:       failed_when: false
   158: 
   159:     - name: Fail with stack diagnostics
   160:       ansible.builtin.fail:
   161:         msg: |-
   162:           prometheus stack failed to deploy/verify on {{ inventory_hostname }}.
   163:           {{ prometheus_stack_diag.results | default([]) | map(attribute='stdout') | join('\n--- next ---\n') }}

name: Decrypt rack_servers from the terraform-proxmox SOPS file
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Seed-bundle stage 1 of 2: READ and VALIDATE the sources.
     3: #
     4: # Split from seed_transform.yml so an agent changing one source does not have to
     5: # read the whole schema transform to find it. Nothing here shapes the bundle; it
     6: # only resolves each source into a parsed fact plus the guards that say whether
     7: # that fact can be trusted.
     8: #
     9: # Sources are independent: the resolved tofu inventory is present on every run,
    10: # while the sibling-repo sources reach the controller only at cutover. Any
    11: # subset produces a valid bundle covering just those slices.
    12: #
    13: # Source shapes: rack_servers (SOPS-encrypted in terraform-proxmox) is known —
    14: # chassis/bmc_ip/bmc_mac/service_tag/mgmt_ip, keyed by node name. VLAN/prefix
    15: # definitions come from a provided JSON var. The fixed-ips.json (tofu-unifi) and
    16: # hosts.yml (ansible-proxmox) mappings are documented ASSUMPTIONS about those
    17: # shapes, isolated here so confirming them is a one-place edit.
    18: #
    19: # Every source is independently optional and contributes only its own slice.
    20: # The seed jobs are additive and tolerate an absent slice (ssot_common.load_seed
    21: # defaults each key to an empty array), so a partial bundle never deletes what
    22: # another source owns. The ONE exception is `drives`, which feeds a sync that
    23: # deletes — see the assert below.
    24: - name: Merge every tofu guest kind into one map
    25:   vars:
    26:     nautobot_seed_tofu: "{{ hostvars['localhost'].tofu_data | default({}, true) }}"
    27:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    28:     nautobot_seed_guests: >-
    29:       {{ (nautobot_seed_tofu.containers | default({}, true))
    30:          | combine(nautobot_seed_tofu.vms | default({}, true))
    31:          | combine(nautobot_seed_tofu.docker_vms | default({}, true))
    32:          | combine(nautobot_seed_tofu.splunk_vm | default({}, true)) }}
    33: 
    34: # Fail only when no source at all would contribute. That writes an empty bundle
    35: # over whatever is already on the guest, which is always an operator mistake.
    36: - name: Assert at least one seed source is available
    37:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    38:     that:
    39:       - >-
    40:         (nautobot_seed_guests | length) > 0
    41:         or (nautobot_seed_networks | length) > 0
    42:         or (nautobot_seed_fixed_ips_path | length) > 0
    43:         or (nautobot_seed_hosts_yml_path | length) > 0
    44:         or (nautobot_seed_sops_path | length) > 0
    45:         or (nautobot_seed_hardware_path | length) > 0
    46:     fail_msg: >-
    47:       nautobot_build_seed is true but no seed source is available: the tofu
    48:       inventory resolved no guests and NAUTOBOT_SEED_NETWORKS,
    49:       TOFU_UNIFI_FIXED_IPS, ANSIBLE_PROXMOX_HOSTS and TERRAFORM_PROXMOX_SOPS
    50:       are all unset. The bundle would be empty.
    51:     quiet: true
    52: 
    53: # Warn per absent source so a thin bundle is never silent.
    54: - name: Warn when an optional seed source is absent
    55:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    56:     msg: >-
    57:       {{ item.env }} is unset — the {{ item.slice }} seed contributes nothing
    58:       this run; existing Nautobot objects of that kind are retained.
    59:   loop:
    60:     - env: TERRAFORM_PROXMOX_SOPS
    61:       slice: DCIM device
    62:       missing: "{{ (nautobot_seed_sops_path | length) == 0 }}"
    63:     - env: TOFU_UNIFI_FIXED_IPS
    64:       slice: IP reservation
    65:       missing: "{{ (nautobot_seed_fixed_ips_path | length) == 0 }}"
    66:     - env: ANSIBLE_PROXMOX_HOSTS
    67:       slice: pve node
    68:       missing: "{{ (nautobot_seed_hosts_yml_path | length) == 0 }}"
    69:     - env: INT_HOMELAB_HARDWARE
    70:       slice: hardware device and module
    71:       missing: "{{ (nautobot_seed_hardware_path | length) == 0 }}"
    72:     - env: ANSIBLE_PROXMOX_DRIVES
    73:       slice: physical drive
    74:       missing: "{{ (nautobot_seed_drives_path | length) == 0 }}"
    75:   loop_control:
    76:     label: "{{ item.env }}"
    77:   when: item.missing | bool
    78: 
    79: # --- Read + decrypt the sources on the controller --------------------------
    80: - name: Decrypt rack_servers from the terraform-proxmox SOPS file
    81:   ansible.builtin.command:
    82:     cmd: "sops -d {{ nautobot_seed_sops_path }}"
    83:   delegate_to: localhost
    84:   become: false
    85:   vars:
    86:     ansible_become: false
    87:   changed_when: false
    88:   register: nautobot_seed_sops_raw
    89:   when: nautobot_seed_sops_path | length > 0
    90:   no_log: true
    91: 
    92: - name: Read the tofu-unifi fixed-IP reservations
    93:   ansible.builtin.slurp:
    94:     src: "{{ nautobot_seed_fixed_ips_path }}"
    95:   delegate_to: localhost
    96:   become: false
    97:   vars:
    98:     ansible_become: false
    99:   register: nautobot_seed_fixed_ips_raw
   100:   when: nautobot_seed_fixed_ips_path | length > 0
   101: 
   102: - name: Read the generated hardware inventory slice
   103:   ansible.builtin.slurp:
   104:     src: "{{ nautobot_seed_hardware_path }}"
   105:   delegate_to: localhost
   106:   become: false
   107:   vars:
   108:     ansible_become: false
   109:   register: nautobot_seed_hardware_raw
   110:   when: nautobot_seed_hardware_path | length > 0
   111: 
   112: - name: Read the ansible-proxmox physical drive inventory
   113:   ansible.builtin.slurp:
   114:     src: "{{ nautobot_seed_drives_path }}"
   115:   delegate_to: localhost
   116:   become: false
   117:   vars:
   118:     ansible_become: false
   119:   register: nautobot_seed_drives_raw
   120:   when: nautobot_seed_drives_path | length > 0
   121: 
   122: - name: Read the ansible-proxmox hosts inventory
   123:   ansible.builtin.slurp:
   124:     src: "{{ nautobot_seed_hosts_yml_path }}"
   125:   delegate_to: localhost
   126:   become: false
   127:   vars:
   128:     ansible_become: false
   129:   register: nautobot_seed_hosts_raw
   130:   when: nautobot_seed_hosts_yml_path | length > 0
   131: 
   132: # Each parse is gated on the same path variable that gated its read, so an
   133: # absent source yields an empty document without ever touching the register a
   134: # skipped task left behind.
   135: - name: Parse the sources
   136:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   137:     nautobot_seed_rack_servers: >-
   138:       {{ (nautobot_seed_sops_raw.stdout | default('{}', true) | from_json).rack_servers | default({}) }}
   139:     nautobot_seed_fixed_ips: >-

   173: # is a pass-through, not a transform. Guarding on the key rather than trusting
   174: # the file: a truncated or wrong-shaped YAML would otherwise reach the job as a

   179:       # `is defined` alone does NOT do what this guard is for: a key present

name: Install the sshd CA drop-in
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # ssh_ca_trust (VM/guest half) — pinned-fingerprint CA fetch, trust file,
     3: # principals map, sshd drop-in with EFFECTIVE-config assertion, and a static
     4: # break-glass lockout guard. Sibling of the ansible-proxmox role (PVE + LXC);
     5: # keep shapes in lockstep. Live-touch tasks skip under Docker (molecule).
     6: 
     7: - name: Assert the pinned CA fingerprint and OpenBao address are present
     8:   ansible.builtin.assert:
     9:     that:
    10:       - ssh_ca_trust_ca_fingerprint | length > 0
    11:       - ssh_ca_trust_bao_addr | length > 0
    12:     fail_msg: >-
    13:       ssh_ca_trust needs SSH_CA_FINGERPRINT (the pinned CA fingerprint from
    14:       the openbao converge's trusted ceremony) and BAO_ADDR. Refusing to
    15:       distribute trust without a pin — that would be trust-on-first-use.
    16:   when: ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
    17:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
    18: 
    19: - name: Assert the host clock is NTP-synchronized
    20:   ansible.builtin.command:
    21:     cmd: timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value
    22:   register: ssh_ca_trust_ntp
    23:   changed_when: false
    24:   failed_when: ssh_ca_trust_ntp.stdout != 'yes'
    25:   when:
    26:     - ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
    27:     - ansible_virtualization_type != 'docker'
    28:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
    29: 
    30: - name: Fetch the CA public key from OpenBao
    31:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    32:     url: "{{ ssh_ca_trust_bao_addr }}/v1/{{ ssh_ca_trust_mount }}/public_key"
    33:     return_content: true
    34:     follow_redirects: all
    35:   register: ssh_ca_trust_fetched
    36:   when: ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
    37:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
    38: 
    39: - name: Compute the fetched CA key's fingerprint
    40:   ansible.builtin.shell:
    41:     executable: /bin/bash
    42:     cmd: >-
    43:       set -o pipefail;
    44:       printf '%s\n' "{{ ssh_ca_trust_fetched.content | trim }}"
    45:       | ssh-keygen -l -f /dev/stdin | awk '{print $2}'
    46:   register: ssh_ca_trust_fetched_fp
    47:   changed_when: false
    48:   when: ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
    49:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
    50: 
    51: - name: Verify the fetched CA key against the pinned fingerprint (fail closed)
    52:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    53:     that:
    54:       - ssh_ca_trust_fetched_fp.stdout == ssh_ca_trust_ca_fingerprint
    55:     fail_msg: >-
    56:       CA public key fingerprint mismatch — fetched
    57:       {{ ssh_ca_trust_fetched_fp.stdout }} but the pin is
    58:       {{ ssh_ca_trust_ca_fingerprint }}. Possible endpoint substitution or an
    59:       unrecorded CA rotation. NOT writing trust.
    60:   when: ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
    61:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
    62: 
    63: - name: Write the trusted CA keys file
    64:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    65:     dest: "{{ ssh_ca_trust_ca_file }}"
    66:     content: |
    67:       {{ ([ssh_ca_trust_fetched.content | trim] + ssh_ca_trust_extra_ca_keys) | join('\n') }}
    68:     owner: root
    69:     group: root
    70:     mode: "0644"
    71:   when: ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
    72:   notify: Reload sshd
    73:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
    74: 
    75: - name: Create the principals directory
    76:   ansible.builtin.file:
    77:     path: "{{ ssh_ca_trust_principals_dir }}"
    78:     state: directory
    79:     owner: root
    80:     group: root
    81:     mode: "0755"
    82:   when: ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
    83:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
    84: 
    85: - name: Write the per-user principals files
    86:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    87:     dest: "{{ ssh_ca_trust_principals_dir }}/{{ item.key }}"
    88:     content: |
    89:       {{ item.value | join('\n') }}
    90:     owner: root
    91:     group: root
    92:     mode: "0644"
    93:   loop: "{{ ssh_ca_trust_principals | dict2items }}"
    94:   loop_control:
    95:     label: "{{ item.key }}: {{ item.value | join(', ') }}"
    96:   when: ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
    97:   notify: Reload sshd
    98:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
    99: 
   100: - name: Install the sshd CA drop-in
   101:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   102:     dest: "{{ ssh_ca_trust_dropin }}"
   103:     content: |
   104:       # Managed by ansible-proxmox-apps ssh_ca_trust — OpenBao SSH client CA
   105:       # trust (ssh-certificate-authority ADR). Late-numbered to win merges.
   106:       TrustedUserCAKeys {{ ssh_ca_trust_ca_file }}
   107:       AuthorizedPrincipalsFile {{ ssh_ca_trust_principals_dir }}/%u
   108:     owner: root
   109:     group: root
   110:     mode: "0644"
   111:     validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
   112:   when:
   113:     - ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
   114:     - ansible_virtualization_type != 'docker'
   115:   notify: Reload sshd
   116:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
   117: 
   118: - name: Read the effective sshd configuration
   119:   ansible.builtin.command:
   120:     cmd: sshd -T
   121:   register: ssh_ca_trust_effective
   122:   changed_when: false
   123:   when:
   124:     - ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
   125:     - ansible_virtualization_type != 'docker'
   126:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
   127: 
   128: - name: Assert the effective sshd config trusts the CA and principals map
   129:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   130:     that:
   131:       - ("trustedusercakeys " ~ ssh_ca_trust_ca_file) in ssh_ca_trust_effective.stdout
   132:       - ("authorizedprincipalsfile " ~ ssh_ca_trust_principals_dir ~ "/%u") in ssh_ca_trust_effective.stdout
   133:     fail_msg: >-
   134:       sshd -T does not show the CA trust directives — another config fragment
   135:       is overriding the drop-in. Effective config must win before certs work.
   136:   when:
   137:     - ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
   138:     - ansible_virtualization_type != 'docker'
   139:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]
   140: 
   141: # Lockout guard: the converge user's static key is the break-glass secondary
   142: # (ADR hybrid rule) until WS4 rotates it — never strand a guest.
   143: - name: Assert a static authorized_key still exists for the converge user
   144:   ansible.builtin.command:
   145:     cmd: grep -cE '^(ssh|ecdsa)-' "/home/{{ ansible_user | default('debian') }}/.ssh/authorized_keys"
   146:   register: ssh_ca_trust_static_keys
   147:   changed_when: false
   148:   failed_when: ssh_ca_trust_static_keys.stdout | int < 1
   149:   when:
   150:     - ssh_ca_trust_enabled | bool
   151:     - ansible_virtualization_type != 'docker'
   152:   tags: [ssh_ca_trust]

review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: #
     3: # These tasks build /etc contents that will be copied to the target filesystem
     4: # to override the default configs of the respective packages and system parts.
     5: #
     6: # We copy Jinja2 templates (from ../templates) and static files (from ../files).
     7: # Files are simply copied, templates are rendered and then written to /etc.
     8: #
     9: # Symlinks can be used for individual files, but not for directories.
    10: # If symlinks were used for directories too, we couldn't tell whether the
    11: # symlink target is a file or a directory - Ansible doesn't seem to let us.
    12: #
    13: # Possible future additions:
    14: # - preserve permissions
    15: # - ability to remove files, not just to add or change/override them
    16: # - collapse files/ into templates/ and treat everything as a template
    17: #
    18: 
    19: - name: Create /etc directories for template output
    20:   tags: always
    21:   file:
    22:     path: "{{ configs_dir }}/etc/{{ item.path }}"
    23:     state: directory
    24:     mode: "755"
    25:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/templates/' + role) }}"
    26:   when: item.state == 'directory'
    27:   loop_control:
    28:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    29: 
    30: - name: Create /etc directories for static files
    31:   tags: always
    32:   file:
    33:     path: "{{ configs_dir }}/etc/{{ item.path }}"
    34:     state: directory
    35:     mode: "755"
    36:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/files/' + role) }}"
    37:   when: item.state == 'directory'
    38:   loop_control:
    39:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    40: 
    41: - name: Render /etc templates
    42:   tags: always
    43:   template:
    44:     src: "{{ item.root }}/{{ item.path }}"
    45:     dest: "{{ configs_dir }}/etc/{{ item.path | regex_replace('.j2$', '') }}"
    46:     mode: "644"
    47:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/templates/' + role) }}"
    48:   when: item.path is regex('\.j2$')
    49:   loop_control:
    50:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    51: 
    52: - name: Copy /etc static files
    53:   tags: always
    54:   copy:
    55:     src: "{{ item.root }}/{{ item.path }}"
    56:     dest: "{{ configs_dir }}/etc/{{ item.path }}"
    57:     mode: "preserve"
    58:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/files/' + role) }}"
    59:   when: (not item.path is regex('\.j2$')) and (item.state == 'file' or item.state == 'link')
    60:   loop_control:

    63: - name: Create rootfs directories for static files

    66:     path: "{{ configs_dir }}/{{ item.path }}"
    67:     state: directory
    68:     mode: "755"
    69:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/rootfs/' + role, errors='ignore') }}"
    70:   when: item.state == 'directory'
    71:   loop_control:
    72:     label: "{{ item.path }}"

    78:     dest: "{{ configs_dir }}/{{ item.path }}"

    80:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/rootfs/' + role, errors='ignore') }}"
    81:   when: (not item.path is regex('\.j2$')) and (item.state == 'file' or item.state == 'link')

    14:       raw: systemctl is-system-running --wait

    16:       changed_when: false
    17:

    19:     - name: Check Python2 is installed
    20:       raw: python2 -c 'import sys; print(sys.version_info[1])'
    21:       ignore_errors: yes
    22:       register: python2_version
    23:       changed_when: false
    24: 
    25:     - name: Check Python3 is installed
    26:       raw: python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.version_info[1])'
    27:       ignore_errors: yes
    28:       register: python3_version

    30: 
    31:     - name: Bootstrap with python Debian/Ubuntu

    33:       ignore_errors: yes
    34:       register: python_install
    35:       changed_when: python_install.stdout_lines|length > 1
    36:       when: (python2_version is failed and python3_version is failed) or python3_version.stdout|int < 5
    37: 
    38:     - name: Link correct python version in Ubuntu 14
    39:       raw: ls /usr/bin/python3.5 && sudo rm -f /usr/bin/python3 && sudo ln -s /usr/bin/python3.5 /usr/bin/python3
    40:       when: python3_version is success and python3_version.stdout|int < 5
    41:       ignore_errors: yes
    42: 
    43:     - name: Bootstrap with python RedHat/CentOS
    44:       raw: sudo yum install -y python3
    45:       ignore_errors: yes
    46:       register: python_install
    47:       changed_when: python_install.stdout_lines|length > 1
    48:       when: python2_version is failed and python3_version is failed
    49:

    51:       command: sudo yum install -y python3 python3-dnf
    52:       ignore_errors: yes
    53:

    56:       ignore_errors: yes
    57:       register: python_install
    58:       changed_when: python_install.stdout_lines|length > 1
    59:       when: python2_version is failed and python3_version is failed

    62:       raw: ls /usr/bin/python || { ls /usr/bin/python3 && ln -s /usr/bin/python3 /usr/bin/python; } || { ls /usr/bin/python2 && ln -s /usr/bin/python2 /usr/bin/python; }
    63:       become: yes
    64:       ignore_errors: yes
    65: 
    66:     # In case of redhat systems libselinux-python3 is needed

    69:       become: yes
    70:       ignore_errors: yes
    71:

    75: 
    76:       become: yes

    83:       ignore_errors: yes
    84:

    88:       become: yes

    97:     - name: Add the authorized_key to the nodes again
    98:       lineinfile: dest="/home/{{ansible_user}}/.ssh/authorized_keys" line="{{ lookup('file', pk_file) }}2"
    99:       ignore_errors: yes
   100:

   103:

   106:       when: ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"
   107:       ignore_errors: yes
   108:       register: apt_update
   109:       become: yes

   111:       async: 120
   112:       poll: 1

   117:       ignore_errors: yes
   118:       become: yes
   119:       become_method: sudo
   120:       async: 120
   121:       poll: 1

review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Headless full-lifecycle reprovision to local-disk boot.
     3: #   1. Pin NFS on the router + cycle into it (safe state for wiping
     4: #      local disks).
     5: #   2. Assert / is NFS-rooted; cross-binding validate armbian_local_disks.
     6: #   3. disk_provision each disk.
     7: #   4. Pin local on the router + cycle into it.
     8: #
     9: # Requires per host: armbian_local_disks (list of disk_binding dicts).
    10: # Usage:
    11: #   ansible-playbook playbooks/armbian/reprovision_to_local.yaml \
    12: #     -i igou-inventory/inventory.yaml -e target_hosts=orange-pi-5-max-01
    13: - name: 1a. Pin NFS boot mode on the router
    14:   ansible.builtin.import_playbook: converge_boot_mode.yaml
    15:   vars:
    16:     armbian_boot_mode: nfs
    17: 
    18: - name: 1b. Cycle board into NFS before wiping local disks
    19:   ansible.builtin.import_playbook: cycle_board.yaml
    20:   vars:
    21:     armbian_boot_mode: nfs
    22: 
    23: - name: 2-3. Cross-binding validate + provision each disk
    24:   hosts: "{{ target_hosts | default('boards') }}"
    25:   gather_facts: true
    26:   gather_subset: [mounts]
    27:   pre_tasks:
    28:     - name: Assert / is on NFS before wiping anything
    29:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    30:         that: >-
    31:           ansible_mounts | selectattr('mount', 'equalto', '/')
    32:           | map(attribute='fstype') | first in ['nfs', 'nfs4']
    33:         fail_msg: "Board must be NFS-booted before reprovisioning local disks."
    34: 
    35:     - name: Cross-binding validate - no two disks share a mount path
    36:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    37:         that:
    38:           - >-
    39:             (armbian_local_disks | map(attribute='layout') | flatten
    40:              | selectattr('mount', 'defined') | map(attribute='mount') | list | length)
    41:             ==
    42:             (armbian_local_disks | map(attribute='layout') | flatten
    43:              | selectattr('mount', 'defined') | map(attribute='mount') | list | unique | length)
    44:         fail_msg: >-
    45:           Two or more disks declare the same mount path. Mount paths:
    46:           {{ armbian_local_disks | map(attribute='layout') | flatten | selectattr('mount', 'defined') | map(attribute='mount') | list }}

    48:     - name: Cross-binding validate - exactly one '/' across all disks

    52:         fail_msg: >-
    53:           Expected exactly one partition with mount: / across all
    54:           armbian_local_disks; found
    55:           {{ armbian_local_disks | map(attribute='layout') | flatten | selectattr('mount', 'equalto', '/') | list | length }}.

name: Query current UPS service configuration
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Configure the TrueNAS built-in UPS service as a NUT netclient (SLAVE)
     3: # against the upsmonitor Pi's NUT netserver (igou-inventory#124).
     4: #
     5: # The Pi (10.10.9.32) drives both rack UPSes over USB and its upsd already
     6: # serves VLAN9 with a `monitor` secondary account
     7: # (igou-ansible playbooks/upsmonitor/setup-nut.yml, upsd.users.j2).
     8: # TrueNAS joins as a netclient and walks its own shutdown sequence
     9: # (VMs get their shutdown_timeout, then services, then poweroff) when the
    10: # monitored UPS reaches the configured shutdown condition.
    11: #
    12: # midclt ups.* is used directly — no arensb module manages the UPS service
    13: # config; arensb.truenas.service handles enable/start.
    14: #
    15: # Variables (igou-inventory group_vars/truenas.yml):
    16: #   truenas_ups — {identifier, remotehost, remoteport?, shutdown?,
    17: #                  shutdowntimer?, monuser, monitor_password_lookup}
    18: #   monitor_password_lookup is the full 1Password lookup expression; this
    19: #   play only consumes the value (igou-inventory#772).
    20: - name: Configure TrueNAS UPS netclient against the upsmonitor Pi
    21:   hosts: truenas
    22:   gather_facts: false
    23:   become: false
    24:   tasks:
    25: 
    26:     - name: Assert UPS variables are present
    27:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    28:         that:
    29:           - truenas_ups is defined
    30:           - truenas_ups.identifier is defined
    31:           - truenas_ups.remotehost is defined
    32:           - truenas_ups.monuser is defined
    33:           - truenas_ups.monitor_password_lookup is defined
    34:         fail_msg: >-
    35:           truenas_ups must define identifier, remotehost, monuser and
    36:           monitor_password_lookup (see igou-inventory group_vars/truenas.yml).
    37: 
    38:     - name: Query current UPS service configuration
    39:       ansible.builtin.command: midclt call ups.config
    40:       register: truenas_ups_query
    41:       changed_when: false
    42:       check_mode: false
    43:       no_log: true  # config carries monpwd
    44: 
    45:     - name: Project desired UPS configuration
    46:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    47:         truenas_ups_desired:
    48:           mode: SLAVE
    49:           identifier: "{{ truenas_ups.identifier }}"
    50:           remotehost: "{{ truenas_ups.remotehost }}"
    51:           remoteport: "{{ truenas_ups.remoteport | default(3493) }}"
    52:           shutdown: "{{ truenas_ups.shutdown | default('LOWBATT') }}"
    53:           shutdowntimer: "{{ truenas_ups.shutdowntimer | default(30) }}"
    54:           monuser: "{{ truenas_ups.monuser }}"
    55:           monpwd: "{{ truenas_ups.monitor_password_lookup }}"
    56:       no_log: true
    57: 
    58:     - name: Update UPS service configuration
    59:       vars:
    60:         truenas_ups_in_sync: >-
    61:           {{ (truenas_ups_query.stdout | from_json
    62:               | dict2items
    63:               | selectattr('key', 'in', truenas_ups_desired.keys() | list)
    64:               | items2dict) == truenas_ups_desired }}
    65:       ansible.builtin.command:
    66:         argv:
    67:           - midclt
    68:           - call
    69:           - ups.update
    70:           - "{{ truenas_ups_desired | to_json }}"
    71:       when: not truenas_ups_in_sync
    72:       changed_when: true
    73:       no_log: true
    74: 
    75:     - name: Enable and start the UPS service
    76:       arensb.truenas.service:
    77:         name: ups
    78:         enabled: true
    79:         state: started
    80: 
    81:     - name: Verify the monitored UPS is reachable through upsd
    82:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
    83:         upsc {{ truenas_ups.identifier }}@{{ truenas_ups.remotehost }}:{{
    84:           truenas_ups.remoteport | default(3493) }} ups.status
    85:       register: truenas_ups_upsc
    86:       changed_when: false
    87:       # upsmon needs a few seconds after a config change / service start.
    88:       retries: 5
    89:       delay: 5
    90:       until: truenas_ups_upsc.rc == 0
    91: 
    92:     - name: Report UPS status
    93:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    94:         msg: "{{ truenas_ups.identifier }}: {{ truenas_ups_upsc.stdout }}"

name: Run podman auto-update (pull newer images, restart updated units)
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Roll rootless podman workloads to fresh images. `podman auto-update` pulls a
     3: # newer image for every container whose quadlet sets AutoUpdate=registry and
     4: # restarts that unit (rolling back if the restarted unit fails to come up, the
     5: # podman default). Containers without the label are left untouched, so opting a
     6: # workload in/out is a one-line change in its linux_podman_quadlet_specs entry.
     7: #
     8: # Variables:
     9: #   linux_podman_run_as_user - rootless user that owns the workloads (host_vars)
    10: #   podman_auto_update_prune - also prune dangling images afterwards so the
    11: #                              VPS disk doesn't fill with stale layers
    12: #                              (default true)
    13: - name: Update rootless podman workload images (podman auto-update)
    14:   hosts: "{{ ansible_limit | default('vps') }}"
    15:   become: true
    16:   gather_facts: false
    17: 
    18:   vars:
    19:     _run_user: "{{ linux_podman_run_as_user | default('igou') }}"
    20:     _rootless_env:
    21:       XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: "/run/user/{{ getent_passwd[_run_user][1] }}"
    22:       HOME: "/home/{{ _run_user }}"
    23: 
    24:   tasks:
    25:     - name: Resolve the run user's uid (for the rootless podman runtime dir)
    26:       ansible.builtin.getent:
    27:         database: passwd
    28:         key: "{{ _run_user }}"
    29: 
    30:     - name: Run podman auto-update (pull newer images, restart updated units)
    31:       ansible.builtin.command:
    32:         cmd: podman auto-update --format json
    33:       become: true
    34:       become_user: "{{ _run_user }}"
    35:       environment: "{{ _rootless_env }}"
    36:       register: _auto_update
    37:       # podman prints `null` (or nothing) when no container carries the
    38:       # autoupdate label; a real run yields a list whose Updated field is
    39:       # "true" for units that were rolled to a new image.
    40:       changed_when: >-
    41:         'true' in (((_auto_update.stdout or 'null') | from_json or [])
    42:                    | map(attribute='Updated') | list)
    43: 
    44:     - name: Report what was updated
    45:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    46:         msg: >-
    47:           {{ _results if _results | length > 0
    48:              else 'No containers opted in (AutoUpdate=registry) or no updates available.' }}
    49:       vars:
    50:         _results: "{{ (_auto_update.stdout or 'null') | from_json or [] }}"
    51: 
    52:     - name: Prune dangling images left behind by the update
    53:       ansible.builtin.command:
    54:         cmd: podman image prune --force
    55:       become: true
    56:       become_user: "{{ _run_user }}"
    57:       environment: "{{ _rootless_env }}"
    58:       register: _prune
    59:       changed_when: _prune.stdout | length > 0
    60:       when: podman_auto_update_prune | default(true) | bool

name: Stop the running hermes user units for a consistent archive
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Weekly hermes state backup -> rustfs-cold (igou-io/igou-inventory#155).
     3: #
     4: # Quiesces the hermes user units (only the ones actually running - a
     5: # deliberately-stopped dashboard stays stopped), tars ~hermes/.hermes with
     6: # numeric ownership (the VM uses keep-id UID mapping; restores must
     7: # preserve exact uids), restarts the units, then uploads the archive from
     8: # the EE to ONE fixed key in the versioned hermes-backups bucket on
     9: # rustfs-cold. Each weekly run becomes the new current version; the
    10: # bucket's ILM rule (NewerNoncurrentVersions: 3, declared in igou-inventory
    11: # host_vars/rustfs-cold.yml) retains exactly the current + 3 previous
    12: # copies. Until ILM enforcement is verified live (#155 checklist), old
    13: # versions may accumulate - harmless, revisit after ~5 runs.
    14: #
    15: # The tarball contains ~/.hermes/.env (live secrets): the bucket is
    16: # reachable only by the hermes-backups user (policy-scoped to this bucket)
    17: # and root keys. At-rest encryption of the tarball is an open question in
    18: # #155 - not implemented here.
    19: #
    20: # Credentials: 1Password item hermes-backups-rustfs-cold (lab_s3 vault),
    21: # resolved at runtime - the job template must carry the
    22: # onepassword-connect-token credential. The endpoint comes from the same
    23: # inventory host_vars the rustfs_state role reconciles against.
    24: #
    25: # Restore:
    26: #   1. aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket hermes-backups \
    27: #        --prefix hermes/dot-hermes.tar.gz   (pick a VersionId)
    28: #   2. aws s3api get-object --version-id <id> ... dot-hermes.tar.gz
    29: #   3. systemctl --user stop hermes-gateway hermes-dashboard (as hermes)
    30: #   4. tar xzf --numeric-owner -C /home/hermes .hermes ; re-assert (members are .hermes/... — the operand ./.hermes matches nothing)
    31: #      0700 on /home/hermes ; systemctl --user start ...
    32: - name: Back up hermes state to rustfs-cold
    33:   hosts: "{{ ansible_limit | default('hermes-hermes') }}"
    34:   gather_facts: false
    35:   become: true
    36:   vars:
    37:     hermes_user: hermes
    38:     hermes_home: /home/hermes
    39:     hermes_state_mount: "{{ hermes_home }}/.hermes"
    40:     hermes_backup_quiesce_units:
    41:       - hermes-gateway.service
    42:       - hermes-dashboard.service
    43:     # Single source of truth: the rustfs-cold stub host's spec vars.
    44:     hermes_s3_endpoint: "{{ hostvars['rustfs-cold'].rustfs_state_endpoint }}"
    45:     hermes_s3_bucket: hermes-backups
    46:     hermes_s3_object: hermes/dot-hermes.tar.gz
    47:     hermes_s3_region: us-east-1
    48:     hermes_s3_access_key: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'hermes-backups-rustfs-cold', field='username', vault='lab_s3') }}"
    49:     hermes_s3_secret_key: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'hermes-backups-rustfs-cold', field='password', vault='lab_s3') }}"
    50:     # Rebuildable artifacts are excluded: containers/ is the podman
    51:     # graphroot (~10G of images configure re-pulls from the pinned tags),
    52:     # bin/ and node/ are tooling reinstalled by setup-os/configure. Real
    53:     # agent state (hermes-agent, sessions, skills, cron, state-snapshots,
    54:     # logs, .env, dashboard-files, ...) stays in - ~1.2G raw, and the
    55:     # quiesce window stays under a minute instead of the 8 it takes to
    56:     # gzip the podman storage.
    57:     hermes_backup_excludes:
    58:       - .hermes/containers
    59:       - .hermes/bin
    60:       - .hermes/node
    61:       # agent-runtime/tools holds the runtime-pulled coding-agent CLIs
    62:       # (multi-GB, re-fetchable via `agent-update all`); the overlay's small
    63:       # bin/state/bashenv.d stay in so pins and update history survive.
    64:       - .hermes/agent-runtime/tools
    65:     # Real state alone is tens of MB; an implausibly small tarball means
    66:     # the state mount was not mounted - fail rather than upload garbage.
    67:     hermes_backup_min_bytes: 1048576
    68: 
    69:   pre_tasks:
    70:     - name: Resolve the ssh login user (fetch below must read the archive without become)
    71:       ansible.builtin.command:
    72:         argv: [id, -un]
    73:       register: _login_user
    74:       become: false
    75:       changed_when: false
    76: 
    77:     - name: Resolve the hermes service user's uid (user systemd bus needs it)
    78:       ansible.builtin.getent:
    79:         database: passwd
    80:         key: "{{ hermes_user }}"
    81: 
    82:     - name: Stage a control-node scratch path for the fetched archive
    83:       ansible.builtin.tempfile:
    84:         state: file
    85:         suffix: .tar.gz
    86:       register: _local_archive
    87:       delegate_to: localhost
    88:       connection: local
    89:       become: false
    90:       changed_when: false
    91: 
    92:   tasks:
    93:     - name: Quiesce, archive, restart
    94:       block:
    95:         - name: Check which hermes user units are running
    96:           ansible.builtin.command: # noqa: command-instead-of-module
    97:             argv: [systemctl, --user, is-active, "{{ item }}"]
    98:           loop: "{{ hermes_backup_quiesce_units }}"
    99:           register: _unit_state
   100:           changed_when: false
   101:           failed_when: false
   102:           become: true
   103:           become_user: "{{ hermes_user }}"
   104:           environment:
   105:             XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: "/run/user/{{ ansible_facts.getent_passwd[hermes_user][1] }}"
   106: 
   107:         - name: Stop the running hermes user units for a consistent archive
   108:           ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   109:             name: "{{ item.item }}"
   110:             state: stopped
   111:             scope: user
   112:           loop: "{{ _unit_state.results }}"
   113:           loop_control:
   114:             label: "{{ item.item }}"
   115:           when: item.rc == 0
   116:           become: true
   117:           become_user: "{{ hermes_user }}"
   118:           environment:
   119:             XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: "/run/user/{{ ansible_facts.getent_passwd[hermes_user][1] }}"
   120: 
   121:         - name: Stage a guest scratch file for the archive
   122:           ansible.builtin.tempfile:
   123:             state: file
   124:             suffix: .tar.gz
   125:           register: _remote_archive
   126:           changed_when: false
   127: 
   128:         - name: Archive the hermes state directory
   129:           ansible.builtin.command:
   130:             argv: >-
   131:               {{ ['tar', 'czf', _remote_archive.path, '--numeric-owner']
   132:                  + (hermes_backup_excludes | map('regex_replace', '^', '--exclude=') | list)
   133:                  + ['-C', hermes_home, '.hermes'] }}
   134:           changed_when: true
   135: 
   136:         - name: Hand the archive to the login user (a root-owned file forces
   137:             fetch into its slurp fallback - base64 through memory - instead
   138:             of sftp; a 4G archive OOMed that path)
   139:           ansible.builtin.file:
   140:             path: "{{ _remote_archive.path }}"
   141:             owner: "{{ _login_user.stdout }}"
   142:             mode: "0600"
   143:           changed_when: false
   144: 
   145:       always:
   146:         - name: Restart exactly the units that were running
   147:           ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   148:             name: "{{ item.item }}"
   149:             state: started
   150:             scope: user
   151:           loop: "{{ _unit_state.results | default([]) }}"
   152:           loop_control:
   153:             label: "{{ item.item }}"
   154:           when: item.rc | default(1) == 0
   155:           become: true
   156:           become_user: "{{ hermes_user }}"
   157:           environment:
   158:             XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: "/run/user/{{ ansible_facts.getent_passwd[hermes_user][1] }}"
   159: 
   160:     - name: Fetch the archive to the control node
   161:       ansible.builtin.fetch:
   162:         src: "{{ _remote_archive.path }}"
   163:         dest: "{{ _local_archive.path }}"
   164:         flat: true
   165:       become: false
   166: 
   167:     - name: Remove the guest scratch file
   168:       ansible.builtin.file:
   169:         path: "{{ _remote_archive.path }}"
   170:         state: absent
   171:       changed_when: false
   172: 
   173:     - name: Stat the fetched archive
   174:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   175:         path: "{{ _local_archive.path }}"
   176:       register: _archive_stat
   177:       delegate_to: localhost
   178:       connection: local
   179:       become: false
   180: 
   181:     - name: Refuse to upload an implausibly small archive
   182:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   183:         that:
   184:           - _archive_stat.stat.size | int >= hermes_backup_min_bytes | int
   185:         fail_msg: >-
   186:           Archive is {{ _archive_stat.stat.size }} bytes (<
   187:           {{ hermes_backup_min_bytes }}) - was {{ hermes_state_mount }}
   188:           actually mounted?
   189:       delegate_to: localhost
   190:       connection: local
   191:       become: false
   192: 
   193:     - name: Upload the archive as the new current version
   194:       amazon.aws.s3_object:
   195:         endpoint_url: "{{ hermes_s3_endpoint }}"
   196:         access_key: "{{ hermes_s3_access_key }}"
   197:         secret_key: "{{ hermes_s3_secret_key }}"
   198:         region: "{{ hermes_s3_region }}"
   199:         bucket: "{{ hermes_s3_bucket }}"
   200:         object: "{{ hermes_s3_object }}"
   201:         src: "{{ _local_archive.path }}"
   202:         mode: put
   203:         # No canned ACL: the hermes-backups policy grants no ACL verbs and
   204:         # RustFS access control is IAM-policy based - the module's default
   205:         # (permission: [private]) makes a separate PutObjectAcl call after
   206:         # a multipart upload, which 403s.
   207:         permission: []
   208:       # RustFS 1.0.0-beta.8 miscomputes CRC32 on UploadPart, so the default
   209:       # integrity checksums boto3 >= 1.36 sends (2025-01 behavior change)
   210:       # fail every multipart part with "Io error: checksum mismatch: CRC32".
   211:       # when_required is the documented escape hatch for third-party stores.
   212:       environment:
   213:         AWS_REQUEST_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION: when_required
   214:         AWS_RESPONSE_CHECKSUM_VALIDATION: when_required
   215:       delegate_to: localhost
   216:       connection: local
   217:       become: false
   218: 
   219:     - name: Read back the uploaded object's metadata
   220:       amazon.aws.s3_object_info:
   221:         endpoint_url: "{{ hermes_s3_endpoint }}"
   222:         access_key: "{{ hermes_s3_access_key }}"
   223:         secret_key: "{{ hermes_s3_secret_key }}"
   224:         region: "{{ hermes_s3_region }}"
   225:         bucket_name: "{{ hermes_s3_bucket }}"
   226:         object_name: "{{ hermes_s3_object }}"
   227:       register: _uploaded
   228:       delegate_to: localhost
   229:       connection: local
   230:       become: false
   231: 
   232:     - name: Record the backup outcome
   233:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   234:         msg: >-
   235:           Uploaded {{ _archive_stat.stat.size }} bytes to
   236:           s3://{{ hermes_s3_bucket }}/{{ hermes_s3_object }}
   237:           (version {{ _uploaded.object_info[0].object_data.version_id
   238:                       | default('n/a') }})
   239: 
   240:   post_tasks:
   241:     - name: Remove the control-node scratch file
   242:       ansible.builtin.file:
   243:         path: "{{ _local_archive.path }}"
   244:         state: absent
   245:       delegate_to: localhost
   246:       connection: local
   247:       become: false
   248:       changed_when: false

name: Remaster ISO to no-prompt boot media (extract → preflight → swap → repack)
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Publish the Microsoft Evaluation Center Windows ISO library on
     3: # public.igou.systems AND emit no-prompt (remastered) siblings for the golden
     4: # pipeline's unattended install feedstock.
     5: #
     6: # Design: igou-io/igou-ansible#343 (Windows golden-image design v3, increment 1);
     7: # publish leg originally from igou-io/igou-openshift#380 Phase 1.
     8: #
     9: # ── Publish leg ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    10: # The nginx-reverse-proxy container on TrueNAS serves /mnt/ssd/public read-only
    11: # at public.igou.systems (autoindex), so the ISOs under
    12: # /mnt/ssd/public/isos/windows/ are published with zero nginx config changes:
    13: #   https://public.igou.systems/isos/windows/<file>.iso   (and http:// for CDI)
    14: #
    15: # ASSUMPTION (not a task): the vanilla eval ISO library and its SHA256SUMS
    16: # already live at /mnt/ssd/public/isos/windows/ on TrueNAS. This play does NOT
    17: # transfer anything — it only asserts presence + integrity of the serving copy.
    18: # igounas (Synology) remains the archival provenance of the media, but that is
    19: # background, not a runtime dependency: no igounas connectivity is needed here.
    20: #
    21: # One-time seed procedure for adding a NEW eval ISO to the library (run by hand
    22: # ON TrueNAS, then add the file to truenas_windows_isos below):
    23: #   1. Copy the ISO into the served dir. igounas DSM has no sftp/scp, so stream
    24: #      it over ssh (cat) from TrueNAS:
    25: #        ssh igou@igounas.igou.systems \
    26: #          "cat /volume1/igoushare/Lab/isos/windows/<file>.iso" \
    27: #          > /mnt/ssd/public/isos/windows/<file>.iso
    28: #   2. Append the upstream checksum line to the manifest:
    29: #        echo "<sha256>  <file>.iso" >> /mnt/ssd/public/isos/windows/SHA256SUMS
    30: # Thereafter this play verifies it on every run.
    31: #
    32: # ── Remaster leg (why noprompt media exists) ───────────────────────────────
    33: # Windows install media stops at a "Press any key to boot from CD…" prompt.
    34: # For a fully declarative KubeVirt build the firmware must NOT wait: with a
    35: # no-keypress firmware the prompting cdboot.efi makes the firmware SKIP the CD
    36: # and boot-loop a blank disk. Microsoft ships (undocumented) efisys_noprompt.bin
    37: # / cdboot_noprompt.efi variants; swapping them in and repacking the ISO yields
    38: # media that boots straight into Setup. This is the only declarative path
    39: # (matches Red Hat's pipeline) — see #343 review. TrueNAS SCALE has no native
    40: # xorriso, so the whole remaster runs inside a throwaway pinned docker container
    41: # that has /isos bind-mounted.
    42: #
    43: # This playbook runs fine from the devcontainer: the only network path it needs
    44: # is devcontainer → truenas SSH (truenas_admin@truenas.igou.systems).
    45: 
    46: - name: Publish Windows eval ISOs on public.igou.systems
    47:   hosts: truenas
    48:   gather_facts: false
    49:   become: false
    50:   vars:
    51:     # Serving location on TrueNAS; override in group_vars/truenas.yml as needed.
    52:     truenas_public_pool: ssd
    53:     # Refquota bump is OPT-IN: the live ssd/public dataset deliberately runs
    54:     # refquota=none (pool has ample headroom). Set a BYTE COUNT (int, e.g.
    55:     # 161061273600 for 150GiB) to enforce one; empty skips the task.
    56:     truenas_public_quota: ""
    57:     truenas_windows_isos:
    58:       - winserver2025-eval-en-us.iso
    59:       - winserver2022-eval-en-us.iso
    60:       - winserver2019-eval-en-us.iso
    61:       - winserver2016-eval-en-us.iso
    62:       - win11-25h2-enterprise-eval-en-us.iso
    63:       - win11-ltsc2024-enterprise-eval-en-us.iso
    64:       - win11-iot-ltsc2024-enterprise-eval-en-us.iso
    65:     _dst_dir: "/mnt/{{ truenas_public_pool }}/public/isos/windows"
    66:   tasks:
    67: 
    68:     - name: Bump the public dataset refquota (headroom for the ISO library)
    69:       # arensb.truenas.filesystem takes refquota as an integer byte count.
    70:       when: truenas_public_quota | string | length > 0
    71:       arensb.truenas.filesystem:
    72:         name: "{{ truenas_public_pool }}/public"
    73:         state: present
    74:         type: FILESYSTEM
    75:         refquota: "{{ truenas_public_quota | int }}"
    76:       tags: [quota]
    77: 
    78:     - name: Ensure the published ISO directory exists
    79:       ansible.builtin.file:
    80:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}"
    81:         state: directory
    82:         mode: "0755"
    83:       tags: [dir]
    84: 
    85:     - name: Stat each published ISO
    86:       # Presence of the vanilla library is an assumption, not a task — assert it.
    87:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    88:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item }}"
    89:       register: _iso_stat
    90:       loop: "{{ truenas_windows_isos }}"
    91:       loop_control:
    92:         label: "{{ item }}"
    93:       tags: [verify]
    94: 
    95:     - name: Assert every listed ISO is present in the serving directory
    96:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    97:         that: item.stat.exists
    98:         fail_msg: >-
    99:           {{ item.item }} is missing from {{ _dst_dir }}. This play assumes the
   100:           vanilla ISO library is already seeded there; add it via the one-time
   101:           seed procedure documented in this file's header (stream from igounas
   102:           over ssh cat, then append its line to SHA256SUMS).
   103:       loop: "{{ _iso_stat.results }}"
   104:       loop_control:
   105:         label: "{{ item.item }}"
   106:       tags: [verify]
   107: 
   108:     - name: Read the SHA256SUMS manifest
   109:       # Slurp once and parse in Jinja (the house idiom — Play 2 slurps its
   110:       # markers) instead of spawning a grep per ISO. A missing manifest fails
   111:       # here, loudly, before the presence assertion below.
   112:       ansible.builtin.slurp:
   113:         src: "{{ _dst_dir }}/SHA256SUMS"
   114:       register: _sums_raw
   115:       tags: [verify]
   116: 
   117:     - name: Assert every listed ISO has a line in SHA256SUMS
   118:       # `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` (below) passes SILENTLY for files that have no
   119:       # line in the manifest, so this explicit presence check is required: an ISO
   120:       # missing from the manifest must fail loudly. Strip the "<hash>  " prefix
   121:       # from each manifest line to get the filename list, then assert membership.
   122:       vars:
   123:         _sums_files: >-
   124:           {{ (_sums_raw.content | b64decode).splitlines()
   125:              | map('regex_replace', '^[0-9A-Fa-f]+ +', '')
   126:              | map('trim') | select | list }}
   127:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   128:         that: item in _sums_files
   129:         fail_msg: >-
   130:           {{ item }} has no line in {{ _dst_dir }}/SHA256SUMS. This play assumes
   131:           the vanilla ISO library is already seeded there; add its checksum line
   132:           via the one-time seed procedure documented in this file's header
   133:           (append "<sha256>  {{ item }}" to SHA256SUMS).
   134:       loop: "{{ truenas_windows_isos }}"
   135:       loop_control:
   136:         label: "{{ item }}"
   137:       tags: [verify]
   138: 
   139:     - name: Verify checksums on the serving copy (hard gate)
   140:       # DEFENDED command (no native equivalent): this verifies EVERY line of the
   141:       # checksum manifest against the files on disk, including the <base>-noprompt
   142:       # siblings the remaster play (Play 2) appends — filenames that no play var
   143:       # enumerates. A native stat get_checksum comparison could only cover the
   144:       # ISOs listed in truenas_windows_isos and would silently ignore those
   145:       # appended remaster lines; no module verifies an arbitrary checksum-manifest
   146:       # file wholesale. Runs before the remaster play; on a fresh system the
   147:       # -noprompt lines are not yet present (only the pristine ISOs are checked),
   148:       # on a converged system both are present and checked.
   149:       ansible.builtin.command:
   150:         cmd: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
   151:         chdir: "{{ _dst_dir }}"
   152:       register: _sha
   153:       changed_when: false
   154:       failed_when: _sha.rc != 0
   155:       tags: [verify]
   156: 
   157: # ── Remaster leg ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   158: # become: true because docker requires root on TrueNAS SCALE (matches the docker
   159: # tasks in configure_docker_containers.yml). Extraction/repack happen in a pinned
   160: # throwaway container; only the idempotence decision, marker write, checksum and
   161: # SHA256SUMS update happen on the host (per #343: lineinfile, hash on host).
   162: 
   163: - name: Emit no-prompt remastered Windows ISOs
   164:   hosts: truenas
   165:   gather_facts: false
   166:   become: true
   167:   vars:
   168:     truenas_public_pool: ssd
   169:     # The two standing golden-pipeline editions. The other 5 remain publishable
   170:     # (above) but unremastered by default; add to this list to remaster them.
   171:     windows_iso_remaster:
   172:       - winserver2025-eval-en-us.iso
   173:       - win11-25h2-enterprise-eval-en-us.iso
   174:     _dst_dir: "/mnt/{{ truenas_public_pool }}/public/isos/windows"
   175:     # Scratch on the same dataset as the ISOs (plenty of space); cleaned up after.
   176:     _scratch: "/mnt/{{ truenas_public_pool }}/public/isos/windows/.remaster-work"
   177:     # Pinned by digest (skopeo-resolved alpine:3.20, 2026-07-11); xorriso via apk.
   178:     # Digest pin makes the remaster reproducible and supply-chain-auditable.
   179:     _remaster_image: >-
   180:       docker.io/library/alpine:3.20@sha256:d9e853e87e55526f6b2917df91a2115c36dd7c696a35be12163d44e6e2a4b6bc
   181:     # The full remaster, run inside the container. $1 = base ISO filename.
   182:     #   1. extract the ISO tree WITHOUT loop-mounting (unprivileged-friendly)
   183:     #   2. preflight (MUST): hard-fail unless BOTH noprompt boot files exist
   184:     #   3. swap the prompting boot files for the noprompt variants
   185:     #   4. repack with the verified official flags (-iso-level 4 packs the >4GB
   186:     #      install.wim; do NOT add -udf)
   187:     _remaster_script: |
   188:       set -eu
   189:       # 7zip reads the UDF tree (where Windows media stores everything but a
   190:       # stub README in ISO9660 — xorriso -osirrox extracts only that ISO9660
   191:       # view and misses efi/, sources/install.wim, boot/); xorriso does the
   192:       # bootable repack. Both are unprivileged, no loop mount, no KVM.
   193:       apk add --no-cache 7zip xorriso >/dev/null
   194:       base="$1"
   195:       src="/isos/${base}"
   196:       tree="/work/${base%.iso}"
   197:       rm -rf "$tree"
   198:       mkdir -p "$tree"
   199:       7z x -bd -bso0 -bsp0 -o"$tree" "$src"
   200:       bootdir="$tree/efi/microsoft/boot"
   201:       # Per-ISO preflight: some media lack the shipped-but-undocumented noprompt
   202:       # boot files. Refuse to produce a silently-still-prompting ISO.
   203:       if [ ! -f "$bootdir/efisys_noprompt.bin" ] || [ ! -f "$bootdir/cdboot_noprompt.efi" ]; then
   204:         echo "PREFLIGHT_FAIL: ${base} lacks efisys_noprompt.bin and/or cdboot_noprompt.efi" >&2
   205:         exit 3
   206:       fi
   207:       rm -f "$bootdir/efisys.bin" "$bootdir/cdboot.efi"
   208:       mv "$bootdir/efisys_noprompt.bin" "$bootdir/efisys.bin"
   209:       mv "$bootdir/cdboot_noprompt.efi" "$bootdir/cdboot.efi"
   210:       xorriso -as mkisofs -no-emul-boot -e "efi/microsoft/boot/efisys.bin" \
   211:         -boot-load-size 1 -iso-level 4 -J -l -D -N -joliet-long \
   212:         -relaxed-filenames -V "WINDOWS" \
   213:         -o "/isos/${base%.iso}-noprompt.iso" "$tree"
   214:       rm -rf "$tree"
   215:       echo "REMASTERED ${base}"
   216:   tasks:
   217: 
   218:     - name: Stat published source ISOs (with sha256)
   219:       # Hashing the source each run is the cost of true hash-idempotence: the
   220:       # marker below stores this hash so we re-remaster only when it changes.
   221:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   222:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item }}"
   223:         get_checksum: true
   224:         checksum_algorithm: sha256
   225:       register: _remaster_src
   226:       loop: "{{ windows_iso_remaster }}"
   227:       loop_control:
   228:         label: "{{ item }}"
   229:       tags: [remaster]
   230: 
   231:     - name: Fail if a remaster source ISO is not published
   232:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   233:         that: item.stat.exists
   234:         fail_msg: "Remaster source {{ item.item }} not present in {{ _dst_dir }} — publish it first."
   235:       loop: "{{ _remaster_src.results }}"
   236:       loop_control:
   237:         label: "{{ item.item }}"
   238:       tags: [remaster]
   239: 
   240:     - name: Read existing source-hash markers
   241:       ansible.builtin.slurp:
   242:         src: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso.src.sha256"
   243:       register: _remaster_marker
   244:       loop: "{{ windows_iso_remaster }}"
   245:       loop_control:
   246:         label: "{{ item }}"
   247:       failed_when: false
   248:       tags: [remaster]
   249: 
   250:     - name: Stat existing no-prompt ISOs
   251:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   252:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso"
   253:       register: _remaster_np
   254:       loop: "{{ windows_iso_remaster }}"
   255:       loop_control:
   256:         label: "{{ item }}"
   257:       tags: [remaster]
   258: 
   259:     - name: Decide which ISOs need remastering (skip when noprompt exists AND marker matches source hash)
   260:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   261:         _to_remaster: >-
   262:           {{ (_to_remaster | default([])) + [item.0.item]
   263:              if ((not item.2.stat.exists)
   264:                   or (item.1.content is not defined)
   265:                   or ((item.1.content | b64decode | trim) != item.0.stat.checksum))
   266:              else (_to_remaster | default([])) }}
   267:       loop: "{{ _remaster_src.results | zip(_remaster_marker.results, _remaster_np.results) | list }}"
   268:       loop_control:
   269:         label: "{{ item.0.item }}"
   270:       tags: [remaster]
   271: 
   272:     - name: Report remaster plan
   273:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   274:         msg: "ISOs to (re)remaster this run: {{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   275:       tags: [remaster]
   276: 
   277:     - name: Create the remaster scratch workspace
   278:       ansible.builtin.file:
   279:         path: "{{ _scratch }}"
   280:         state: directory
   281:         mode: "0700"
   282:       when: (_to_remaster | default([])) | length > 0
   283:       tags: [remaster]
   284: 
   285:     - name: Remaster ISO to no-prompt boot media (extract → preflight → swap → repack)
   286:       # DEFENDED command (over community.docker.docker_container): this is a
   287:       # one-shot `docker run --rm` whose exit code AND stdout ARE the result
   288:       # (changed_when keys on 'REMASTERED', PREFLIGHT_FAIL surfaces via rc/stderr);
   289:       # docker_container manages container lifecycle/state and does not cleanly
   290:       # return a throwaway run's captured output and exit status.
   291:       # argv avoids all shell quoting: the script is passed intact, base as $1.
   292:       # A ~8GB ISO takes a few minutes of IO — hence the generous async window.
   293:       # rc != 0 (e.g. PREFLIGHT_FAIL, exit 3) fails the task with the stderr shown.
   294:       ansible.builtin.command:
   295:         argv:
   296:           - docker
   297:           - run
   298:           - --rm
   299:           - --pull=missing
   300:           - -v
   301:           - "{{ _dst_dir }}:/isos"
   302:           - -v
   303:           - "{{ _scratch }}:/work"
   304:           - "{{ _remaster_image }}"
   305:           - sh
   306:           - -c
   307:           - "{{ _remaster_script }}"
   308:           - remaster
   309:           - "{{ item }}"
   310:       register: _remaster_run
   311:       changed_when: "'REMASTERED' in _remaster_run.stdout"
   312:       # No async: `command` has no default timeout, so it waits out the
   313:       # multi-minute IO on its own. The async wrapper was swallowing the
   314:       # container's stdout/stderr and failing the task with an opaque rc=38.
   315:       loop: "{{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   316:       loop_control:
   317:         label: "{{ item }}"
   318:       tags: [remaster]
   319: 
   320:     - name: Record the source-hash marker for each remastered ISO
   321:       # The marker sibling stores the SOURCE hash; the decide step above compares
   322:       # it to re-remaster only when the pristine ISO is refreshed.
   323:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   324:         content: "{{ (_remaster_src.results | selectattr('item', 'equalto', item) | first).stat.checksum }}\n"
   325:         dest: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso.src.sha256"
   326:         mode: "0644"
   327:       loop: "{{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   328:       loop_control:
   329:         label: "{{ item }}"
   330:       tags: [remaster]
   331: 
   332:     - name: World-readable perms on remastered ISOs (match the served dir)
   333:       ansible.builtin.file:
   334:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso"
   335:         mode: "0644"
   336:       loop: "{{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   337:       loop_control:
   338:         label: "{{ item }}"
   339:       tags: [remaster]
   340: 
   341:     - name: Compute sha256 of remastered ISOs
   342:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   343:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso"
   344:         get_checksum: true
   345:         checksum_algorithm: sha256
   346:       register: _remaster_np_sha
   347:       loop: "{{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   348:       loop_control:
   349:         label: "{{ item }}"
   350:       tags: [remaster]
   351: 
   352:     - name: Update SHA256SUMS with the remastered ISO hashes (idempotent by filename)
   353:       ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
   354:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/SHA256SUMS"
   355:         regexp: "  {{ (item.item[:-4] ~ '-noprompt.iso') | regex_escape }}$"
   356:         line: "{{ item.stat.checksum }}  {{ item.item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso"
   357:         create: true
   358:         mode: "0644"
   359:       loop: "{{ _remaster_np_sha.results }}"
   360:       loop_control:
   361:         label: "{{ item.item }}"
   362:       tags: [remaster]
   363: 
   364:     - name: Remove the remaster scratch workspace
   365:       ansible.builtin.file:
   366:         path: "{{ _scratch }}"
   367:         state: absent
   368:       tags: [remaster]

     4: - name: Install iptables-persistent
     5:   become: true
     6:   apt:
     7:     name: iptables-persistent
     8:     state: latest
     9:     update_cache: true
    10: 
    11: - name: Gather service facts
    12:   become: true
    13:   service_facts:
    14: 
    15: - name: Copy rules.v4
    16:   become: true
    17:   template:
    18:     src: rules_{{ firewall_hostgroup }}.v4.j2
    19:     dest: /etc/iptables/rules.v4
    20:     mode: "644"
    21:   register: copy4
    22: 
    23: - name: Copy rules.v6
    24:   become: true
    25:   template:
    26:     src: rules_{{ firewall_hostgroup }}.v6.j2
    27:     dest: /etc/iptables/rules.v6
    28:     mode: "644"
    29:   register: copy6
    30: 
    31: # Only reload when the rule set actually changed. `iptables-restore` without `--noflush`
    32: # replaces the whole *filter and *nat tables, which also removes the chains Docker installs
    33: # at daemon start (DOCKER, DOCKER-USER, DOCKER-FORWARD, ...) and the nat MASQUERADE rule for
    34: # the bridge network. Reloading unconditionally therefore broke container networking on every
    35: # repeat run of this role.
    36: #
    37: # These deliberately are not handlers: the reload has to happen before the Docker check below,
    38: # while handlers only run at the end of the play. Using `meta: flush_handlers` instead would
    39: # also fire pending handlers of earlier roles, which is not what we want here.
    40: - name: Load IPv4 rules # noqa: no-handler
    41:   become: true
    42:   shell: "iptables-restore < /etc/iptables/rules.v4"
    43:   when: copy4.changed
    44: 
    45: - name: Load IPv6 rules # noqa: no-handler
    46:   become: true
    47:   shell: "ip6tables-restore < /etc/iptables/rules.v6"
    48:   when: copy6.changed
    49: 
    50: # Docker only installs its iptables rules when the daemon starts, so it cannot recover on its
    51: # own once they have been flushed. Restart it whenever they are missing. This doubles as a
    52: # self-heal for hosts where the rules were already lost by an earlier run.
    53: - name: Check whether Docker's iptables rules are present
    54:   become: true
    55:   command: iptables -t nat -S POSTROUTING
    56:   register: docker_nat_rules
    57:   changed_when: false
    58:   failed_when: false
    59:   check_mode: false
    60:   when: "'docker.service' in ansible_facts.services"
    61: 
    62: - name: Restart docker to reinstall its iptables rules
    63:   become: true
    64:   service:
    65:     name: docker
    66:     state: restarted
    67:   when:
    68:     - "'docker.service' in ansible_facts.services"
    69:     - docker_nat_rules.stdout is defined
    70:     - "'MASQUERADE' not in docker_nat_rules.stdout"

    30: # `apps` with `available_apps` definitions. This is useful to had metadata to

    56: #           ]
    57: #         }
    58: #       ]
    59: #     }

    63: #     {
    64: #       "name": "richie",
    65: #       "services": [
    66: #         {
    67: #           "name": "postgresql",
    68: #           "host": "pg.foo.com",
    69: #           "templates": [

    71: #             "apps/richie/templates/postgresql/ep.yml.j2",
    72: #             "apps/richie/templates/postgresql/svc.yml.j2"
    73: #           ]
    74: #         }
    75: #       ]
    76: #     }

    79:     available_apps: "{{ lookup('apps', apps_paths) }}"

    95:   register: merged_apps

    97: 
    98: - name: Set applications for this namespace

   102: - name: Display enriched applications definitions (apps)

name: Create the config maps in k8s
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Create ConfigMaps for an app
     3: 
     4: # First we create ConfigMaps dedicated to be used as a volume in a DeploymentContfig [1]
     5: # Then we will deal with ConfigMaps dedicated to be used as environment variables [2]
     6: #
     7: # [1] https://docs.okd.io/latest/dev_guide/configmaps.html#configmaps-use-case-consuming-in-volumes
     8: # [2] https://docs.okd.io/latest/dev_guide/configmaps.html#configmaps-use-case-consuming-in-env-vars
     9: 
    10: ################# Generic ConfigMaps #######################
    11: - name: Create generic config maps
    12:   kubernetes.core.k8s:
    13:     definition: "{{ lookup('template', item) | from_yaml_all }}"
    14:     state: present
    15:   with_items: "{{ configmaps }}"
    16:   when: configmaps is defined
    17:   tags: configmap
    18: 
    19: ################# ConfigMaps used in a volume #######################
    20: 
    21: # Select services with ConfigMaps
    22: - name: Set ConfigMaps for application {{ app.name }}
    23:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    24:     app_configmaps: "{{ app | json_query('services[?configs].{name: name, configs: configs}') }}"
    25: 
    26: # Create the configmaps dictionnary:
    27: #
    28: # - each key of this dictionnary is a service name
    29: # - the corresponding value is the ConfigMap for this service (a dictionnary):
    30: #     - each key of this dictionnary is a file name
    31: #     - the corresponding value is the file content (rendered template)
    32: #
    33: # An example follows:
    34: #
    35: # {
    36: #   "nginx": {
    37: #       "cms.conf": "...",
    38: #       "lms.conf": "..."
    39: #   }
    40: # }
    41: - name: Format configMaps
    42:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    43:     configmaps_from_files: |
    44:       {%- set configmaps_from_files = {} -%}
    45:       {%- for service in app_configmaps -%}
    46:         {%- set _ = configmaps_from_files.update({service.name: {}}) -%}
    47:         {%- for cm_path in service.configs -%}
    48:           {%- set content = lookup('template', cm_path, convert_data=False) -%}
    49:           {%- set filename = cm_path | basename | regex_replace('.j2') -%}
    50:           {%- set _ = configmaps_from_files.get(service.name).update({filename: content}) -%}
    51:         {%- endfor -%}
    52:       {%- endfor -%}
    53:       {{ configmaps_from_files }}
    54: 
    55: - name: Display config maps
    56:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    57:     var: configmaps_from_files
    58:     verbosity: 3
    59: 
    60: - name: Create the config maps in k8s
    61:   kubernetes.core.k8s:
    62:     state: present
    63:     name: "{{ app.name }}-{{ item.key }}{{ deployment_stamp is none | ternary('', '-') }}{{ deployment_stamp }}"
    64:     namespace: "{{ namespace_name }}"
    65:     definition:
    66:       apiVersion: v1
    67:       kind: ConfigMap
    68:       metadata:
    69:         labels:
    70:           app: "{{ app.name }}"
    71:           service: "{{ item.key }}"
    72:           deployment_stamp: "{{ deployment_stamp | default('N/A') }}"
    73:       data: "{{ item.value }}"
    74:   with_dict: "{{ configmaps_from_files }}"
    75: 
    76: ################# ConfigMaps used to populate environment variables #######################
    77: 
    78: # Select services with ConfigMaps
    79: - name: Set environment variables ConfigMaps for application {{ app.name }}
    80:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    81:     app_configmaps: "{{ app | json_query('services[?environment_variables].{name: name, environment_variables: environment_variables}') }}"
    82: 
    83: - name: Create environment variables ConfigMaps
    84:   kubernetes.core.k8s:
    85:     state: present
    86:     name: "{{ app.name }}-{{ item.name }}-dotenv{{ deployment_stamp is none | ternary('', '-') }}{{ deployment_stamp }}"
    87:     namespace: "{{ namespace_name }}"
    88:     definition:
    89:       apiVersion: v1
    90:       kind: ConfigMap
    91:       metadata:
    92:         labels:
    93:           app: "{{ app.name }}"
    94:           service: "{{ item.name }}"
    95:           deployment_stamp: "{{ deployment_stamp | default('N/A') }}"
    96:       data: "{{ lookup('template', item.environment_variables) | from_yaml }}"
    97:   loop: "{{ app_configmaps }}"

1: # Install and configure Galaxy

     5:     msg: "Installing Galaxy version '{{ galaxy_version }}'"
     6: 
     7: - name: Create top-level Galaxy directories

     9:     path='{{ item }}'

    12:   - '{{ galaxy_dir }}'

    19: - name: "Stop if proxy prefix is set but is missing leading slash"

    30: - name: "Install utility scripts"

    32:     src={{ item }}

    36:   - "cleanup_dir.sh"
    37:   - "manage_db_backups.sh"
    38: 
    39: - name: "Clone Galaxy source"

    43:     dest: '{{ galaxy_root }}'

    46:     PATH: '/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_env.PATH }}'

    50:     path='{{ item }}'

    79: 
    80: - name: "Determine Python executable for setting up virtualenev"

    82:     python_exe: "{{ galaxy_python_dir }}/bin/python{{ galaxy_python_version.split('.')[:2] | join('.') }}"

    89: - name: "Deal with existing virtualenv in Galaxy root"

    96:     - name: "Get virtualenv Python version"

   173: - name: "Reinstate old conda environments and packages"

   203:     path: '{{ galaxy_root }}/.venv/bin/hg'
