     9:     contains: "controller_credentials:"
    10:     read_whole_file: true
    11:     recurse: true
    12:   register: __list_files_controller_credentials
    13: 
    14: - name: "Read Credentials definitions"
    15:   ansible.builtin.include_vars:
    16:     file: "{{ __read_credentials_definitions_item.path }}"
    17:   loop: "{{ __list_files_controller_credentials.files }}"
    18:   loop_control:
    19:     loop_var: __read_credentials_definitions_item
    20:   register: __contents_filetree_controller_credentials
    21:   failed_when: "'VARIABLE IS NOT DEFINED' in __contents_filetree_controller_credentials"
    22: 
    23: - name: "Populate Credentials Data Structure"
    24:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:

    26:       {{
    27:         __contents_filetree_controller_credentials.results |
    28:         rejectattr('ansible_facts.controller_credentials', 'undefined') |

name: Mark GPU driver policy as checked
review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Detect and classify an existing package-managed or manual amdgpu DKMS driver.
     3: # A stock inbox amdgpu module is intentionally not an installed DKMS release:
     4: # on a fresh node Bloom replaces it with the production 31.40 DKMS driver.
     5: 
     6: - name: Read installed amdgpu-dkms package version
     7:   shell: "dpkg-query -W -f='${Version}' amdgpu-dkms 2>/dev/null || true"
     8:   register: gpu_driver_detected_package
     9:   changed_when: false
    10: 
    11: - name: Read existing amdgpu DKMS registrations
    12:   shell: "dkms status -m amdgpu 2>/dev/null || true"
    13:   register: gpu_driver_detected_dkms
    14:   changed_when: false
    15: 
    16: - name: Detect host ROCm runtime packages
    17:   shell: |
    18:     dpkg-query -W -f='${Package}\n' 2>/dev/null \
    19:       | grep -E '^(rocm($|-hip|-language|-opencl|-ml)|hip-runtime-amd$|amdrocm[0-9]|amdrocm-(core-sdk|runtime))' \
    20:       || true
    21:   register: gpu_driver_detected_rocm_packages
    22:   changed_when: false
    23: 
    24: - name: Initialize GPU driver compatibility matches
    25:   set_fact:
    26:     gpu_driver_compatibility_matches: []
    27: 
    28: - name: Match installed GPU driver against validated tuples
    29:   set_fact:
    30:     gpu_driver_compatibility_matches: "{{ gpu_driver_compatibility_matches + [item] }}"
    31:   loop: "{{ gpu_driver_supported }}"
    32:   loop_control:
    33:     label: "amdgpu {{ item.DriverRelease }} / ROCm {{ item.PairedROCm }}"
    34:   when: >-
    35:     (
    36:       (gpu_driver_detected_package.stdout | trim) != '' and
    37:       item.DKMSPackageCode in (gpu_driver_detected_package.stdout | trim) and
    38:       item.DKMSModuleVersion in (gpu_driver_detected_package.stdout | trim) and
    39:       item.DKMSBuild in (gpu_driver_detected_package.stdout | trim)
    40:     ) or (
    41:       (gpu_driver_detected_package.stdout | trim) == '' and
    42:       (gpu_driver_detected_dkms.stdout | trim) != '' and
    43:       item.DKMSModuleVersion in gpu_driver_detected_dkms.stdout and
    44:       item.DKMSBuild in gpu_driver_detected_dkms.stdout
    45:     )
    46: 
    47: - name: Resolve existing GPU driver policy state
    48:   set_fact:
    49:     gpu_driver_policy_state: >-
    50:       {{
    51:         ('unvalidated-rocm' if (gpu_driver_detected_rocm_packages.stdout | trim) != '' else 'none')
    52:         if ((gpu_driver_detected_package.stdout | trim) == '' and
    53:             (gpu_driver_detected_dkms.stdout | trim) == '')
    54:         else
    55:         ('supported' if (gpu_driver_compatibility_matches | length) == 1 else 'unsupported')
    56:       }}
    57: 
    58: - name: Resolve supported existing GPU driver tuple
    59:   set_fact:
    60:     gpu_driver_compatibility: "{{ gpu_driver_compatibility_matches | first }}"
    61:   when: gpu_driver_policy_state == 'supported'
    62: 
    63: - name: Check all DKMS registrations are from the matched release
    64:   shell: |
    65:     set -e
    66:     while IFS= read -r line; do
    67:       [ -z "$line" ] && continue
    68:       echo "$line" | grep -F "{{ gpu_driver_compatibility.DKMSModuleVersion }}" >/dev/null
    69:       echo "$line" | grep -F "{{ gpu_driver_compatibility.DKMSBuild }}" >/dev/null
    70:     done <<'EOF'
    71:     {{ gpu_driver_detected_dkms.stdout }}
    72:     EOF
    73:   register: gpu_driver_dkms_consistent
    74:   changed_when: false
    75:   failed_when: false
    76:   when:
    77:     - gpu_driver_policy_state == 'supported'
    78: 
    79: - name: Reject mixed DKMS releases
    80:   set_fact:
    81:     gpu_driver_policy_state: unsupported
    82:   when:
    83:     - gpu_driver_dkms_consistent is defined
    84:     - gpu_driver_dkms_consistent.rc | default(0) != 0
    85: 
    86: - name: Resolve requested driver installer tuple
    87:   set_fact:
    88:     gpu_driver_version_resolved: "{{ (GPU_DRIVER_VERSION | default('') | trim) if (GPU_DRIVER_VERSION | default('') | trim != '') else gpu_driver_default_version }}"
    89:     gpu_driver_build_resolved: "{{ (GPU_DRIVER_BUILD | default('') | trim) if (GPU_DRIVER_BUILD | default('') | trim != '') else gpu_driver_default_build }}"
    90:     gpu_driver_target_matches: []
    91: 
    92: - name: Match requested installer against validated tuples
    93:   set_fact:
    94:     gpu_driver_target_matches: "{{ gpu_driver_target_matches + [item] }}"
    95:   loop: "{{ gpu_driver_supported }}"

    11:       - FIRST_NODE | bool
    12:       - DOMAIN is defined and DOMAIN != ""

    14:     success_msg: "✓ ClusterForge bootstrap parameters provided"
    15:   when:
    16:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE is defined
    17:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE != "none"
    18:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE != ""
    19:   tags: [clusterforge, deploy_clusterforge]
    20: 
    21: # Nodes are joined first with CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE "none", so a node whose
    22: # Longhorn CSI plugin never came up stays latent — it looks Ready and nothing
    23: # demands a volume from it — until ClusterForge is deployed days later. The
    24: # failure then surfaces as a five-minute `kubectl wait` timeout on
    25: # openbao-init-job, four layers above the actual cause. Checking CSI driver
    26: # registration up front names the bad node instead.
    27: - name: Verify every node has registered the Longhorn CSI driver
    28:   shell: |
    29:     set -o pipefail
    30:     KUBECTL="/var/lib/rancher/rke2/bin/kubectl --kubeconfig /etc/rancher/rke2/rke2.yaml"
    31:     nodes=$($KUBECTL get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}')

    33:     # list, the loop below never runs, and an unchecked cluster reports success.
    34:     if [ -z "$nodes" ]; then
    35:       echo "Could not list nodes to verify Longhorn CSI registration"
    36:       exit 1
    37:     fi
    38:     missing=""
    39:     for node in $nodes; do
    40:       drivers=$($KUBECTL get csinode "$node" -o jsonpath='{.spec.drivers[*].name}' 2>/dev/null)
    41:       case " $drivers " in
    42:         *" driver.longhorn.io "*) ;;
    43:         *) missing="$missing $node" ;;

    47:       echo "Nodes missing driver.longhorn.io:$missing"
    48:       exit 1
    49:     fi
    50:     echo "All nodes have registered driver.longhorn.io"

    58:   failed_when: false

review_question: Should this executable Ansible task be considered excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Configure Splunk server certificate from operator-mounted TLS secret.
     3: # Input: /mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/{tls.crt, tls.key[, ca.crt]}
     4: # Output: bundled PEM at /opt/splunk/etc/auth/splunk-server-bundle.pem
     5: #         CA at /opt/splunk/etc/auth/splunk-server-ca.pem
     6: #         server.conf [sslConfig] configured
     7: 
     8: - name: Generate ephemeral SSL passphrase
     9:   command: >
    10:     python3 -c
    11:     "import secrets, base64; print(base64.b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(40)).decode())"
    12:   register: ssl_passphrase
    13:   changed_when: false
    14:   no_log: true
    15: 
    16: - name: Ensure Splunk auth directory exists
    17:   file:
    18:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth"
    19:     state: directory
    20:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    21:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
    22:     mode: '0700'
    23:   become: yes
    24:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    25: 
    26: - name: Write cert bundle script
    27:   copy:
    28:     dest: /tmp/splunk_bundle_cert.py
    29:     content: |
    30:       from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    31:           load_pem_private_key, Encoding, PrivateFormat, BestAvailableEncryption
    32:       )
    33:       import sys
    34: 
    35:       passphrase = sys.argv[1].encode()
    36:       key_path   = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.key'
    37:       cert_path  = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.crt'
    38:       out_path   = sys.argv[2] + '/etc/auth/splunk-server-bundle.pem'
    39: 
    40:       with open(key_path, 'rb') as f:
    41:           key = load_pem_private_key(f.read(), password=None)
    42: 
    43:       enc_key_pem = key.private_bytes(
    44:           Encoding.PEM,
    45:           PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
    46:           BestAvailableEncryption(passphrase)
    47:       )
    48: 
    49:       with open(cert_path, 'rb') as f:
    50:           cert_pem = f.read()
    51: 
    52:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
    53:           f.write(cert_pem)
    54:           if not cert_pem.endswith(b'\n'):
    55:               f.write(b'\n')
    56:           f.write(enc_key_pem)
    57:     mode: '0700'
    58: 
    59: - name: Encrypt private key and build server cert bundle
    60:   command: >
    61:     python3 /tmp/splunk_bundle_cert.py
    62:     {{ ssl_passphrase.stdout }} {{ splunk.home }}
    63:   become: yes
    64:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    65:   no_log: true
    66: 
    67: - name: Set bundle permissions
    68:   file:
    69:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/splunk-server-bundle.pem"
    70:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    71:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
    72:     mode: '0600'
    73:   become: yes
    74:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    75: 
    76: - name: Check if ca.crt is present in server cert mount
    77:   stat:
    78:     path: /mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/ca.crt
    79:   register: server_ca_file

    83:     server_ca_path: /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem
    84:   when: not server_ca_file.stat.exists

    86: - name: Write CA trust bundle script
    87:   copy:
    88:     dest: /tmp/splunk_build_server_ca_bundle.py
    89:     content: |
    90:       # tls.crt from the operator-mounted secret may contain intermediate
    91:       # certs that are not repeated in ca.crt (e.g. Vault PKI issuers put
    92:       # only the root in ca.crt). Splunk requires the full chain to be
    93:       # present locally in sslRootCAPath -- it does not complete the chain
    94:       # using intermediates presented by the peer during the handshake.
    95:       # Assemble tls.crt's non-leaf certs + ca.crt into one deduplicated
    96:       # trust bundle.
    97:       import sys
    98: 
    99:       tls_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.crt'
   100:       ca_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/ca.crt'
   101:       out_path = sys.argv[1] + '/etc/auth/splunk-server-ca.pem'
   102: 
   103:       def split_pem_certs(data):
   104:           certs = []
   105:           current = []
   106:           for line in data.splitlines(keepends=True):
   107:               if line.strip() == b'-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----':
   108:                   current = [line]
   109:               elif line.strip() == b'-----END CERTIFICATE-----':
   110:                   current.append(line)
   111:                   certs.append(b''.join(current))
   112:                   current = []
   113:               elif current:
   114:                   current.append(line)
   115:           return certs
   116: 
   117:       with open(tls_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   118:           tls_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   119:       chain_certs = tls_certs[1:]  # drop the leaf; keep any presented intermediates/root
   120: 
   121:       with open(ca_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   122:           ca_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   123: 
   124:       seen = set()
   125:       ordered = []
   126:       for cert in chain_certs + ca_certs:
   127:           if cert not in seen:
   128:               seen.add(cert)
   129:               ordered.append(cert)
   130: 
   131:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
   132:           for cert in ordered:
   133:               f.write(cert)
   134:               if not cert.endswith(b'\n'):
   135:                   f.write(b'\n')
   136:     mode: '0700'
   137:   when: server_ca_file.stat.exists

   140:   command: >
   141:     python3 /tmp/splunk_build_server_ca_bundle.py
   142:     {{ splunk.home }}
   143:   become: yes
   144:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   145:   changed_when: true
   146:   when: server_ca_file.stat.exists

   150:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/splunk-server-ca.pem"

   154:   become: yes
   155:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"

   170:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   171:   become: yes
   172:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"

   176:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/server.conf"

   178:     option: sslPassword
   179:     value: "{{ ssl_passphrase.stdout }}"
   180:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   181:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   182:   become: yes
   183:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   184:   no_log: true
   185:   changed_when: false
   186: 
   187: - name: Configure sslRootCAPath in server.conf
   188:   ini_file:
   189:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/server.conf"
   190:     section: sslConfig
   191:     option: sslRootCAPath

   193:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   194:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"

   196:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"

   210: - name: 'update partition table for CentOS 9'

   248:   with_items: "{{ katello_kickstart_templates }}"
   249: 
   250: # Host group

   254:     --name "CentOS 9"
   255:     --product "CentOS"
   256:     --organization "{{ katello_provisioning_organization }}"

   258: 
   259: - name: 'set find centos kickstart repo'

   261:     katello_provisioning_repo_json: "{{ katello_provisioning_repo.stdout|from_json }}"
   262: 
   263: - name: 'find hostgroup Katello CentOS 9'

    53:         name: docker

    72:     - name: install kubelet kubeadm kubectl

   266:

   270:         state: directory

   278:         remote_src: yes

    44:               for rule in $current_rules; do
    45:                 rule_name=$(echo "$rule" | awk '{print $NF}' | sed 's/{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_//')
    46:                 if ! echo "{{ ftp_firewall_rules | map(attribute='name') | list }}" | grep -q "'$rule_name'"; then
